brenton_translation: But thou in thy many mercies didst not appoint them to destruction, and didst not forsake them; for thou art strong, and merciful, and pitiful.

fresh_translation: And now, our God, strong, great, mighty, and fearful, keeping your covenant and your mercy, let not all the toil grow little before you, which found us and our kings and our rulers and our priests and our prophets and our fathers and all your people, from days of kings of Assour until this day.
brenton_translation: And now, O our God, the powerful, the great, the mighty, and the terrible, keeping thy covenant and thy mercy, let not all the trouble seem little in thy sight which has come upon us, and our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our prophets, and our fathers, and upon all thy people, from the days of the kings of Assur even to this day.

fresh_translation: And you are righteous over all things coming upon us, because you did truth, and we sinned.
brenton_translation: But thou art righteous in all the things that come upon us; for thou hast wrought faithfully, but we have greatly sinned.

fresh_translation: And our kings and our rulers and our priests and our fathers did not do your law and did not pay attention to your commandments and your testimonies with which you testified to them.
brenton_translation: And our kings, and our princes, and our priests, and our fathers, have not performed thy law, and have not given heed to thy commandments, and have not kept thy testimonies which thou didst testify to them.

fresh_translation: And they in your kingdom and in your great goodness which you gave to them, and in the broad and fat land which you gave before them, did not serve you and did not turn from their evil practices.
brenton_translation: And they did not serve thee in thy kingdom, and in thy great goodness which thou gavest to them, and in the large and fat land which thou didst furnish before them, and they turned not from their evil devices.

fresh_translation: Behold, we are slaves today, and the land which you gave to our fathers to eat its fruit,
brenton_translation: Behold, we are servants this day, and as for the land which thou gavest to our fathers to eat the fruit of it and the good things of it, behold, we are servants upon it:

fresh_translation: belongs to kings whom you set over us because of our sins, and over our bodies they rule, and over our cattle as is pleasing to them, and we are in great affliction.
brenton_translation: and its produce is abundant for the kings whom thou didst appoint over us because of our sins; and they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, as it pleases them, and we are in great affliction.

fresh_translation: And in all these things we are making a faithful covenant and writing it, and all our rulers, our Levites, and our priests are sealing it.
brenton_translation: And over them that sealed were Neemias the Artasastha, son of Achalia, and Zedekias,

fresh_translation: And among the sealers: Nehemias son of Achalia, and Sedekias,
brenton_translation: the son of Araea, and Azaria, and Jeremia,

fresh_translation: Seraia, Azaria, and Ieremia,
brenton_translation: Phasur, Amaria, Melchia,

fresh_translation: Phassour, Amaria, Melchia,
brenton_translation: Attus, Sebani, Maluch,

fresh_translation: Atous, Sebani, Mallouch,
brenton_translation: Iram, Meramoth, Abdia,

fresh_translation: Iram, Meramoth, Abdia,
brenton_translation: Daniel, Gannathon, Baruch,

fresh_translation: Daniel, Ganathon, Barouch,
brenton_translation: Mesulam, Abia, Miamin,

fresh_translation: Mesoulam, Abia, Miamin,
brenton_translation: Maazia, Belgai, Samaia; these were priests.

fresh_translation: Maazia, Belgai, Samaia. These were priests.
brenton_translation: And the Levites; Jesus the son of Azania, Banaiu of the sons of Enadad, Cadmiel

fresh_translation: And the Levites: Iesous son of Azania, Banaiou from sons of Enadad, Kadmiel,
brenton_translation: and his brethren, Sabania, Oduia, Calitan, Phelia, Anan,

fresh_translation: and his brothers: Sabania, Odouia, Kalita, Pheleia, Anan,
brenton_translation: Micha, Roob, Asebias,

fresh_translation: Micha, Roob, Esebias,
brenton_translation: Zacchor, Sarabia, Sebania,

fresh_translation: Zachor, Sarabia, Sebania,
brenton_translation: Odum, the sons of Banuae.

fresh_translation: Odouia, sons of Banounai.
brenton_translation: The heads of the people; Phoros, Phaath Moab, Elam, Zathuia,

fresh_translation: Rulers of the people: Phoros, Phaathmoab, Elam, Zathouia, sons of
brenton_translation: the sons of Bani, Asgad, Bebai,

fresh_translation: Bani, Asgad, Bēbai,
brenton_translation: Adania, Bagoi, Hedin

fresh_translation: Edania, Bagoi, Edin,
brenton_translation: Ater, Ezekia, Azur,

fresh_translation: Ater, Ezekia, Azour,
brenton_translation: Oduia, Esam, Besi,

fresh_translation: Odouia, Esam, Bēsi,
brenton_translation: Ariph, Anathoth, Nobai,

fresh_translation: Ariph, Anathoth, Nōbai,
brenton_translation: Megaphes, Mesullam, Ezir,

fresh_translation: Magaphēs, Mesoulam, Hezir,
brenton_translation: Mesozebel, Saduc, Jeddua,

fresh_translation: Mesōzebel, Saddouk, Ieddoua,
brenton_translation: Phaltia, Anan, Anaea,

fresh_translation: Phaltia, Anan, Anaia,
brenton_translation: Osee, Anania, Asub,

fresh_translation: Osēe, Anania, Asoub,
brenton_translation: Aloes, Phalai, Sobec,

fresh_translation: Alōēs, Phalai, Sōbēk,
brenton_translation: Reum, Essabana, Maasia,

fresh_translation: Raoum, Esabana, Maasaia,
brenton_translation: and Aia, Aenan, Enam,

fresh_translation: and Aia, Ainam, Anan,
brenton_translation: Maluch, Eram, Baana.

fresh_translation: Mallouch, Heram, Baana.
brenton_translation: And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the porters, the singers, the Nathinim, and every one who drew off from the nations of the land to the law of God, their wives, their sons, their daughters, every one who had knowledge and understanding,

fresh_translation: And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites, the gatekeepers, the singers, the nethinim, and everyone joining from peoples of the land to law of God, their wives, their sons, their daughters, everyone knowing and understanding,
brenton_translation: were urgent with their brethren, and bound them under a curse, and entered into a curse, and into an oath, to walk in the law of God, which was given by the hand of Moses, the servant of God; to keep and to do all the commandments of the Lord, and his judgments, and his ordinances;

fresh_translation: were strengthening themselves upon their brothers, and cursed themselves and entered into a curse and into an oath, to walk in law of God which was given by hand of Moses servant of God, and to keep and do all commandments of the Lord our God and his judgments,
brenton_translation: and that we will not, they said,give our daughters to the people of the land, nor will we take their daughters to our sons.

fresh_translation: and that we would not give our daughters to peoples of the land and would not take their daughters for our sons,
brenton_translation: And as for the people of the land who bring wares and all manner of merchandise to sell on the sabbath-day, we will not buy of them on the sabbath or on the holy day: and we will leave the seventh year, and the exaction of every debt.

fresh_translation: and that from peoples of the land bringing wares and every merchandise on Sabbath day to sell, we would not buy from them on Sabbath and on holy day, and we would leave the seventh year and demand of every hand.
brenton_translation: And we will impose ordinances upon ourselves, to levy on ourselves the third part of a didrachm yearly for the service of the house of our God;

fresh_translation: And we will set commandments upon ourselves, to give upon ourselves a third of a didrachma yearly for service of house of our God,
brenton_translation: the shewbread, and the continual meat-offering, and for the continual whole-burnt-offering, of the sabbaths, of the new moon, for the feast, and for the holy things, and the sin-offerings, to make atonement for Israel, and for the works of the house of our God.

fresh_translation: for bread of the presence and sacrifice of the continual offering and for continual whole burnt offering of the Sabbaths, of the new moons, for the feasts and for the holy things and for the sin offerings to make atonement concerning Israel, and for works of house of our God.
brenton_translation: And we cast lots for the office of wood-bearing, we the priests, and the Levites, and the people, to bring wood into the house of our God, according to the house of our families, at certain set times, year by year, to burn on the altar of the Lord our God, as it is written in the law:

fresh_translation: And we cast lots concerning lot of wood-bearing, the priests and the Levites and the people, to bring into house of our God, to house of our fathers, at appointed times from years, year by year, to burn on altar of the Lord our God as written in the law,
brenton_translation: and to bring the first-fruits of our land, and the first-fruits of the fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house of the Lord:

fresh_translation: and to bring firstfruits of our land and firstfruits of fruit of every tree, year by year, into house of the Lord,
brenton_translation: the first-born of our sons, and of our cattle, as it is written in the law, and the first-born of our herds and of our flocks, to bring to the house of our God, for the priests that minister in the house of our God.

fresh_translation: and the firstborn of our sons and our cattle as written in the law, and firstborn of our cattle and our flocks, to bring into house of our God, to the priests ministering in house of our God,
brenton_translation: And the first-fruits of our corn, and the fruit of every tree, of wine, and of oil, will we bring to the priests to the treasury of the house of God; and a tithe of our land to the Levites: for the Levites themselves shall receive tithes in all the cities of the land we cultivate.

fresh_translation: and the firstfruit of our grains and fruit of every tree, wine and oil, we will bring to the priests into treasury-room of house of God, and tithe of our land to the Levites, and they, the Levites, are tithing in all cities of our service.
brenton_translation: And the priest the son of Aaron shall be with the Levites in the tithe of the Levite: and the Levites shall bring up the tenth part of their tithe to the house of our God, into the treasuries of the house of God.

fresh_translation: And priest son of Aaron shall be with the Levite in tithe of the Levite, and the Levites shall bring up tithe of the tithe into house of our God, into the treasury-rooms, into house of God.
brenton_translation: For the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring into the treasuries the first-fruits of the corn, and wine, and oil; and there are the holy vessels, and the priests, and the ministers, and the porters, and the singers: and we will not forsake the house of our God.

fresh_translation: For into the treasuries sons of Israel and sons of Levi will bring the firstfruits of the grain and the wine and the oil, and there are the holy vessels and the ministering priests and the gatekeepers and the singers, and we will not forsake house of our God.
And rulers of the people settled in Ierousalem, and the rest of the people cast lots to bring one of ten to settle in Ierousalem, the holy city, and nine parts in the cities.
brenton_translation: And the chiefs of the people dwelt in Jerusalem: and the rest of the people cast lots, to bring one of every ten to dwell in Jerusalem the holy city, and nine parts in the other cities.

fresh_translation: And the people blessed all the men freely choosing to settle in Ierousalem.
brenton_translation: And the people blessed all the men that volunteered to dwell in Jerusalem.

fresh_translation: And these are rulers of the province who settled in Ierousalem, while in cities of Iouda each settled in his own holding, in their cities: Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the nethinim, and sons of servants of Salomon.
brenton_translation: Now these are the chiefs of the province who dwelt in Jerusalem, and in the cities of Juda; every man dwelt in his possession in their cities: Israel, the priests, and the Levites, and the Nathinim, and the children of the servants of Solomon.

fresh_translation: And in Ierousalem settled some from sons of Iouda and some from sons of Beniamin. From sons of Iouda: Athaia son of Azia, son of Zacharia, son of Amaria, son of Saphatia, son of Maleleel, from sons of Phares,
brenton_translation: And there dwelt in Jerusalem some of the children of Juda, and of the children of Benjamin. Of the children of Juda; Athaia son of Azia, the son of Zacharia, the son of Samaria, the son of Saphatia, the son of Maleleel, and some of the sons of Phares;

fresh_translation: and Maasia son of Barouch, son of Chalaza, son of Ozia, son of Adaia, son of Ioirib, son of Thēzia, son of the Sēlōnite.
brenton_translation: and Maasia son of Baruch, son of Chalaza, son of Ozia, son of Adaia, son of Joarib, son of Zacharias, son of Seloni.

fresh_translation: All sons of Phares settling in Ierousalem: four hundred sixty-eight mighty men.
brenton_translation: All the sons of Phares who dwelt in Jerusalem were four hundred and sixty-eight men of might.

fresh_translation: And these are sons of Beniamin: Sēlō son of Mesoulam, son of Iōad, son of Phadaia, son of Kōlia, son of Masaia, son of Aithiēl, son of Iesia.
brenton_translation: And these were the children of Benjamin; Selo son of Mesulam, son of Joad, son of Phadaia, son of Coleia, son of Maasias, son of Ethiel, son of Jesia.

fresh_translation: And after him: Gēbi, Sēli, nine hundred twenty-eight.
brenton_translation: And after him Gebe, Seli, nine hundred and twenty-eight.

fresh_translation: And Iōēl son of Zechri was overseer over them, and Ioudas son of Asana was second over the city.
brenton_translation: And Joel son of Zechri was overseer over them: and Juda son of Asana was second in the city.

fresh_translation: From the priests: Iadaia son of Iōirib, Iachin,
brenton_translation: Of the priests: both Jadia son of Joarib, and Jachin.

fresh_translation: Saraia son of Elkia, son of Mesoulam, son of Saddouk, son of Mariōth, son of Aitōb, opposite house of God,
brenton_translation: Saraia, son of Elchia, son of Mesulam, son of Sadduc, son of Marioth, son of Aetoth, was over the house of God.

fresh_translation: and their brothers doing work of the house: Amasi son of Zacharia, son of Phassour, son of Melchia,
brenton_translation: And their brethren doing the work of the house were eight hundred and twenty-two: and Adaia son of Jeroam, son of Phalalia, son of Amasi, son of Zacharia, son of Phassur, son of Melchia,

fresh_translation: heads of fathers: two hundred forty-two. And Amessai son of Esdriēl,
brenton_translation: and his brethren, chiefs of families, two hundred and forty-two: and Amasia son of Esdriel, son of Mesarimith, son of Emmer,

fresh_translation: and his brothers, mighty men of battle: one hundred twenty-eight, and their overseer was Badiēl.
brenton_translation: and his brethren, mighty men of war, a hundred and twenty-eight: and their overseer was Badiel son of one of the great men.

fresh_translation: And from the Levites: Samaia son of Asoub, son of Ezri,
brenton_translation: And of the Levites; Samaia, son of Esricam,

fresh_translation: and Mathania son of Micha and Ōbēd son of Samoui,
brenton_translation: Matthanias son of Micha, and Jobeb son of Samui,

fresh_translation: two hundred eighty-four.
brenton_translation: two hundred and eighty-four.

fresh_translation: And the gatekeepers: Akoub, Telamin, and their brothers: one hundred seventy-two.
brenton_translation: And the porters; Acub, Telamin, and their brethren, a hundred and seventy-two.

fresh_translation: And overseer of the Levites was son of Bani, Ozi, son of Asabia, son of Micha, from sons of Asaph the singers, over against work of house of God.
brenton_translation: And the overseer of the Levites was the son of Bani, son of Ozi, son of Asabia, the son of Micha. Of the sons of Asaph the singers some were over the house of God,

fresh_translation: For command of the king was upon them.
brenton_translation: For so was the king's commandment concerning them.

fresh_translation: And Pathaia son of Basēza was at hand of the king for every matter of the people.
brenton_translation: And Phathaia son of Baseza was in attendance on the king in every matter for the people,

fresh_translation: And toward the farmsteads in their field, some from sons of Iouda settled in Kariatharbok
brenton_translation: and with regard to villages in their country district: and some of the children of Juda dwelt in Cariatharboc,

fresh_translation: and in Iēsou
brenton_translation: and in Jesu,

fresh_translation: and in Beērsabee,
brenton_translation: and in Bersabee:

fresh_translation: and their farmsteads, Lachis and its fields, and they camped in Beērsabee.
brenton_translation: And their villages were Lachis and her hands: and they pitched their tents in Bersabee.

fresh_translation: And sons of Beniamin settled from Gaba, Machamas,
brenton_translation: And the children of Benjamin dwelt from Gabaa to Machmas.

fresh_translation: And from the Levites, divisions of Iouda were for Beniamin.
brenton_translation: And of the Levites there were divisions to Juda and to Benjamin.

fresh_translation: And these are the priests and the Levites who came up with Zorobabel son of Salathiel and Iesou: Saraia, Iermia, Esdra,
brenton_translation: Now these are the priests and the Levites that went up with Zorobabel the son of Salathiel and Jesus: Saraia, Jeremia, Esdra,

fresh_translation: Amaria, Mallouch,
brenton_translation: Amaria, Maluch,

fresh_translation: Sechenia,
brenton_translation: Sechenia.

fresh_translation: These were leaders of the priests and their brothers in days of Iesou.
brenton_translation: These were the chiefs of the priests, and their brethren in the days of Jesus.

fresh_translation: And the Levites: Iesou, Banoui, Kadmiel, Sarabia, Iouda, Machania, over the hands, he and his brothers,
brenton_translation: And the Levites were, Jesus, Banui, Cadmiel, Sarabia, Jodae, Matthania: he was over the bands,

fresh_translation: for the courses.
brenton_translation: and his brethren were appointed to the daily courses.

fresh_translation: And Iesou begot Iōakim, and Iōakim begot Eliasib, and Eliasib begot Iōdae,
brenton_translation: And Jesus begot Joakim, and Joakim begot Eliasib, and Eliasib begot Jodae,

fresh_translation: and Iōdae begot Ionathan, and Ionathan begot Iadou.
brenton_translation: and Jodae begot Jonathan, and Jonathan begot Jadu.

fresh_translation: And in days of Iōakim, his brothers the priests and heads of the fathers were: to Saraia, Maraia; to Iermia, Anania;
brenton_translation: And in the days of Joakim, his brethren the priests and the heads of families were, belonging to Saraia, Amaria; to Jeremia, Anania;

fresh_translation: to Esdra, Mesoulam; to Amaria, Iōanan;
brenton_translation: to Esdra, Mesulam; to Amaria, Joanan;

fresh_translation: to Mallouch, Ionathan; to Sechenia, Iōsēph;
brenton_translation: to Amaluch, Jonathan; to Sechenia, Joseph;

fresh_translation: to Arem, Adnas; to Mariōth, Elkai;
brenton_translation: to Are, Mannas; to Marioth, Elcai;

fresh_translation: to Addai, Zacharias; to Ganathōn, Mosollam;
brenton_translation: to Adadai, Zacharia; to Ganathoth, Mesolam;

fresh_translation: to Abia, Zechri; to Beniamin, in times; to Phēlti,
brenton_translation: to Abia, Zechri; to Miamin, Maadai; to Pheleti, one;

fresh_translation: to Balga, Samoue; to Semeia, Ionathan;
brenton_translation: to Balgas, Samue; to Semia, Jonathan;

fresh_translation: to Iōiarib, Maththanai; to Idia, Ozi;
brenton_translation: to Joarib, Matthanai; to Edio, Ozi;

fresh_translation: to Sallai, Kallai; to Amouk, Abed;
brenton_translation: to Salai, Callai; to Amec, Abed;

fresh_translation: to Elkia, Asabias; to Iedeiou, Nathanael.
brenton_translation: to Elkia, Asabias; to Jedeiu, Nathanael.

fresh_translation: The Levites in days of Eliasib, Iōada, Iōanan, and Iadou were written as heads of fathers, and the priests in reign of Darius the Persian.
brenton_translation: The Levites in the days of Eliasib, Joada, and Joa, and Joanan, and Idua, were recorded heads of families: also the priests, in the reign of Darius the Persian.

fresh_translation: Sons of Levi, heads of fathers, were written in book of words of the days until days of Iōanan son of Elisoub.
brenton_translation: And the sons of Levi, heads of families, were written in the book of the chronicles, even to the days of Joanan son of Elisue.

fresh_translation: And leaders of the Levites were Asabia and Sarabia and Iesou and sons of Kadmiel, and their brothers opposite them, to hymn and praise by command of David man of God, course by course.
brenton_translation: And the heads of the Levites were Asabia, and Sarabia, and Jesu: and the sons of Cadmiel, and their brethren over against them, were to sing hymns of praise, according to the commandment of David the man of God, course by course.

fresh_translation: When I was gathering the gatekeepers.
brenton_translation: When I gathered the porters,

fresh_translation: In days of Iōakim son of Iesou son of Iosedek, and in days of Nehemias and Ezra the priest, the scribe.
brenton_translation: it was in the days of Joakim son of Jesus, son of Josedec, and in the days of Neemia: and Esdras the priest was scribe.

fresh_translation: And at dedication of wall of Ierousalem they sought the Levites in their places, to bring them into Ierousalem to make dedication and rejoicing, in thanksgiving and in songs, with cymbals and stringed instruments and lyres.
brenton_translation: And at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem they sought the Levites in their places, to bring them to Jerusalem, to keep a feast of dedication and gladness with thanksgiving, and they sounded cymbals with songs, and had psalteries and harps.

fresh_translation: And sons of the singers were gathered both from the district round about into Ierousalem and from the farmsteads,
brenton_translation: And the sons of the singers were assembled both from the neighbourhood round about to Jerusalem, and from the villages,

fresh_translation: and from the fields, because the singers built farmsteads for themselves in Ierousalem.
brenton_translation: and from the country: for the singers built themselves villages by Jerusalem.

fresh_translation: And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people and the gatekeepers and the wall.
brenton_translation: And the priests and the Levites purified themselves, and they purified the people, and the porters, and the wall.

fresh_translation: And I brought up rulers of Iouda upon the wall and set two great thanksgiving choirs, and they went to the right upon the wall by the Dung Gate.
brenton_translation: And they brought up the princes of Juda on the wall, and they appointed two great companies for thanksgiving, and they passed on the right hand on the wall of the dung-gate.

fresh_translation: And after them went Hōsaia and half of rulers of Iouda,
brenton_translation: And after them went Osaia, and half the princes of Juda,

fresh_translation: and Azaria, Esdra, and Mesoulam,
brenton_translation: and Azarias, and Esdras, and Mesollam,

fresh_translation: Iouda and Beniamin and Samaia and Iermia,
brenton_translation: and Juda, and Benjamin, and Samaias and Jeremia.

fresh_translation: and from sons of the priests with trumpets, Zacharias son of Ionathan, son of Samaia, son of Mathania, son of Michaia, son of Zakkour, son of Asaph,
brenton_translation: And some of the sons of the priest with trumpets, Zacharias son of Jonathan, son of Samaias, son of Matthania, son of Michaia, son of Zacchur, son of Asaph:

fresh_translation: and his brothers, Samaia and Oziēl, praising in songs of David man of God, and Ezra the scribe before them,
brenton_translation: and his brethren, Samaia, and Oziel, Gelol, Jama, Aia, Nathanael, and Juda, Anani, to praise with the hymns of David the man of God; and Esdras the scribe was before them,

fresh_translation: at Gate of Ain opposite them. They went up on steps of city of David, on ascent of the wall above house of David and as far as Water Gate eastward.
brenton_translation: at the gate, to praise before them, and they went up by the steps of the city of David, in the ascent of the wall, above the house of David, even to the water-gate

fresh_translation: And the second thanksgiving choir was going to meet them, and I after it, and half of the people upon the wall above Tower of Ovens and as far as Broad Wall,
and above Gate of Ephraim and to the Old Gate and to Fish Gate and Tower of Hananeel and as far as Sheep Gate, and they stood in Gate of the Guard.
brenton_translation: of Ephraim, and to the fish-gate, and by the tower of Anameel, and as far as the sheep-gate.

fresh_translation: And the two choirs stood in house of God, and I and half of the generals with me,
and the priests, Eliakim, Maasias, Beniamin, Michaias, Eliōēnai, Zacharias, Ananias, with trumpets,
and Maasias and Semeias and Eleazar and Ozi and Iōanan and Melchias and Ailam and Ezour. And the singers were heard, and they were appointed.
brenton_translation: And the singers were heard, and were numbered.

fresh_translation: And they sacrificed on that day great sacrifices and rejoiced, because God gladdened them greatly, and their wives and their children rejoiced, and rejoicing in Ierousalem was heard from far away.
brenton_translation: And in that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced; for God had made them very joyful: and their wives and their children rejoiced: and the joy in Jerusalem was heard from afar off.

fresh_translation: And on that day men were appointed over the treasury-rooms, for the treasures, the firstfruits, the tithes, and the things gathered in them by rulers of the cities, portions for the priests and for the Levites, because rejoicing was in Iouda over the priests and over the Levites who stood.
brenton_translation: And in that day they appointed men over the treasuries, for the treasures, the first-fruits, and the tithes, and for the chiefs of the cities who were assembled among them, to furnish portions for the priests and Levites: for there was joy in Juda over the priests and over the Levites that waited.

fresh_translation: And they kept charges of their God and charges of the purification and the singers and the gatekeepers, as commands of David and Salomon his son.
brenton_translation: And they kept the charges of their God, and the charges of the purification, and ordered the singers and the porters, according to the commandments of David and his son Solomon.

fresh_translation: For in days of David, Asaph from the beginning was chief of the singers, and there was hymn and praise to God.
brenton_translation: For in the days of David Asaph was originally first of the singers, and they sang hymns and praise to God.

fresh_translation: And all Israel in days of Zorobabel were giving portions of the singers and the gatekeepers, matter of each day on its day, and sanctifying for the Levites, and the Levites sanctifying for sons of Aaron.
brenton_translation: And all Israel in the days of Zorobabel, and in the days of Neemias, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, a daily rate: and consecrated them to the Levites: and the Levites consecrated them to the sons of Aaron.

fresh_translation: On that day it was read in book of Moses in ears of the people, and it was found written in it that Ammanites and Moabites should not enter into assembly of God forever,
brenton_translation: In that day they read in the book of Moses in the ears of the people; and it was found written in it, that the Ammonites and Moabites should not enter into the congregation of God for ever;

fresh_translation: because they did not meet sons of Israel with bread and water, and they hired Balaam against him to curse him, and our God turned the curse into blessing.
brenton_translation: because they met not the children of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them: but our God turned the curse into a blessing.

fresh_translation: And it came to be when they heard the law, they separated every mixed group in Israel.
brenton_translation: And it came to pass, when they heard the law, that they were separated, even every alien in Israel.

fresh_translation: And before this, Eliasib the priest was dwelling in treasury-room of house of our God, being near to Tobia,
brenton_translation: And before this time Eliasib the priest dwelt in the treasury of the house of our God, connected with Tobias;

fresh_translation: and he made for him a great treasury-room, and there they formerly gave the manna and the frankincense and the vessels and the tithe of grain and wine and oil, the command for the Levites and the singers and the gatekeepers, and firstfruits of the priests.
brenton_translation: and he made himself a great treasury, and there they were formerly in the habit of bestowing the offerings, and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithe of the corn, and the wine, and the oil, the ordered portion of the Levites, and singers, and porters; and the first-fruits of the priests.

fresh_translation: And in all this I was not in Ierousalem, because in thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king, and after end of days I asked leave from the king.
brenton_translation: But in all this time I was not in Jerusalem; for in the thirty-second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon I came to the king, and after a certain time I made my request of the king;

fresh_translation: And I came to Ierousalem and understood the evil which Eliasib did for Tobia, making for him a treasury-room in court of house of God.
brenton_translation: and I came to Jerusalem, and I understood the mischief which Eliasib had done in the case of Tobias, in making for him a treasury in the court of the house of God.

fresh_translation: And it seemed very evil to me, and I threw all vessels of house of Tobia outside the treasury-room.
brenton_translation: And it appeared very evil to me: so I cast forth all the furniture of the house of Tobias from the treasury.

fresh_translation: And I said, and they purified the treasury-rooms, and I restored there vessels of house of God, the manna, and the frankincense.
brenton_translation: And I gave orders, and they purified the treasuries: and I restored thither the vessels of the house of God, and the offerings, and the frankincense.

fresh_translation: And I knew that portions of the Levites had not been given, and the Levites and the singers doing the work fled, each man to his own field.
brenton_translation: And I understood that the portion of the Levites had not been given: and they had fled every one to his field, the Levites and the singers doing the work.

fresh_translation: And I contended with the generals and said, Why was house of God forsaken? And I gathered them and set them in their standing.
brenton_translation: And I strove with the commanders, and said, Wherefore has the house of God been abandoned? and I assembled them, and set them in their place.

fresh_translation: And all Iouda brought tithe of the grain and the wine and the oil into the treasuries.
brenton_translation: And all Juda brought a tithe of the wheat and the wine and the oil into the treasuries,

fresh_translation: Over hand of Selemia the priest and Saddouk the scribe and Phadaia from the Levites, and over their hand Hanan son of Zakkour son of Mathania, because they were reckoned faithful to divide to their brothers.
brenton_translation: to the charge of Selemia the priest, and Sadoc the scribe, and Phadaea of the Levites: and next to them was Anan the son of Zacchur, son of Matthanias; for they were accounted faithful: it was their office to distribute to their brethren.

fresh_translation: Remember me, O God, in this, and let not my mercy be wiped out, which I did in house of Lord God.
brenton_translation: Remember me, O God, in this, and let not my kindness be forgotten which I have wrought in regard to the house of the Lord God.

fresh_translation: In those days I saw in Iouda men treading winepresses on the Sabbath and bringing sheaves and loading them on the donkeys, and wine and grapes and figs and every burden, and bringing them into Ierousalem on Sabbath day, and I testified on day of their selling.
brenton_translation: In those days I saw in Juda men treading wine-presses on the sabbath, and carrying sheaves, and loading asses with both wine, and grapes, and figs, and every kind of burden, and bringing them into Jerusalem on the sabbath-day:

fresh_translation: And they were dwelling in it, bringing fish and every kind of merchandise, selling on the Sabbath to sons of Iouda and in Ierousalem.
brenton_translation: and I testified in the day of their sale. Also their dwelt in it men bringing fish, and selling every kind of merchandise to the children of Juda and in Jerusalem on the sabbath.

fresh_translation: And I contended with sons of Iouda, the free men, and said to them, What is this evil word which you are doing and profaning the Sabbath day?
brenton_translation: And I strove with the free children of Juda, and said to them, What is this evil thing which ye do, and profane the sabbath-day?

fresh_translation: Did not your fathers do thus, and our God brought all these evils upon them and upon us and upon this city? And you add wrath upon Israel by profaning the Sabbath.
brenton_translation: Did not your fathers thus, and our God brought upon them and upon us and upon this city all these evils? and do ye bring additional wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath?

fresh_translation: And it came to be when gates of Ierousalem were set before the Sabbath, I gave word and they shut the gates, and I said that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. And from my servants I set some over the gates, so that no burden be brought in on Sabbath day.
brenton_translation: And it came to pass, when the gates were set up in Jerusalem, before the sabbath, that I spoke, and they shut the gates; and I gave orders that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and I set some of my servants at the gates, that none should bring in burdens on the sabbath-day.

fresh_translation: And all the traders and sellers of merchandise lodged outside Ierousalem once and twice.
brenton_translation: So all the merchants lodged, and carried on traffic without Jerusalem once or twice.

fresh_translation: And I testified among them and said to them, Why do you lodge opposite the wall? If you do this a second time, I will stretch out my hand against you. From that time they did not come on the Sabbath.
brenton_translation: Then I testified against them, and said to them, Why do ye lodge in front of the wall? if ye do so again, I will stretch out my hand upon you. From that time they came not on the sabbath.

fresh_translation: And I told the Levites, those being purified and coming to guard the gates, to sanctify the Sabbath day. Concerning these things remember me, O God, and spare me according to abundance of your mercy.
brenton_translation: and I told the Levites who were purifying themselves, and came and kept the gates, that they should sanctify the sabbath-day. Remember me, O God, for these things, and spare me according to the abundance of thy mercy.

fresh_translation: And in those days I saw the Ioudaioi who had seated Ashdodite, Ammonite, and Moabite women.
brenton_translation: And in those days I saw the Jews who had married women of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:

fresh_translation: And half of their sons were speaking Ashdodite and were not recognizing how to speak Ioudaian.
brenton_translation: and their children spoke half in the language of Ashdod, and did not know how to speak in the Jewish language.

fresh_translation: And I contended with them and cursed them and struck men among them and made them bald, and made them swear by God that you will not give your daughters to their sons and will not take from their daughters for your sons.
brenton_translation: And I strove with them and cursed them; and I smote some of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying,Ye shall not give your daughters to their sons, and ye shall not take of their daughters to your sons.

fresh_translation: Did not Salomon king of Israel sin thus? And among many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by God, and God gave him as king over all Israel, yet foreign women turned even him aside.
brenton_translation: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin thus? though there was no king like him among many nations, and he was beloved of God, and God made him king over all Israel; yet strange women turned him aside.

fresh_translation: And shall we listen to you to do all this evil, to act faithlessly toward our God, seating foreign women?
brenton_translation: So we will not hearken to you to do all this evil, to break covenant with our God, —to marry strange wives.

fresh_translation: And from sons of Iōada, of Elisoub the great priest, was son-in-law of Sanaballat the Horonite, and I drove him out from me.
brenton_translation: and Elisub the high priest, one of the sons of Joada, being son-in-law of Sanaballat the Uranite, I chased him away from me.

fresh_translation: Remember them, O God, for kinship with the priesthood and covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
brenton_translation: Remember them, O God, for their false connection with the priesthood, and the breaking the covenant of the priesthood, and for defiling the Levites.

fresh_translation: And I purified them from every foreign thing and set courses for the priests and for the Levites, each man as his work,
brenton_translation: So I purged them from all foreign connection, and established courses for the priests and the Levites, every man according to his work.

fresh_translation: and gift of the wood-bearers at appointed times from years and in the firstfruits. Remember me, our God, for goodness.
brenton_translation: And the offering of the wood-bearers was at certain set times, and in the times of the first-fruits. Remember me, O our God, for good.

fresh_translation: And it came to be after these words, in days of Artaxerxes, this Artaxerxes ruled from India over one hundred twenty-seven provinces.
In those days, when King Artaxerxes was enthroned in Sousa the city,
in third year of his reign he made a feast for his friends and the rest of the nations and the nobles of Persia and Media and rulers of the satrapies,
and after this, after showing them wealth of his kingdom and glory of joy of his riches for one hundred eighty days,
when days of the marriage were fulfilled, the king made a drinking-feast for the nations found in the city for six days, in court of house of the king,

adorned with linen and carbasus stretched on linen and purple cords, on rings of gold and silver, on marble pillars, and couches of gold and silver on pavement of emerald stone and pearl and marble stone, and coverings transparent and variously flowered, with roses scattered around.
And golden and silver cups, and a carbuncle cup set forth worth thirty thousand talents. Wine was much and sweet, which the king himself drank.
And this drinking was not according to fixed law, for thus the king willed, and he ordered the stewards to do his pleasure and that of the men.
And Astin the queen made a drinking-feast for the women in the royal house where King Artaxerxes was.
And on the seventh day, when the king became merry, he said to Aman and Bazan and Tharra and Borazē and Zatholtha and Abataza and Tharaba, the seven eunuchs serving King Artaxerxes,
to bring in the queen to him, to crown her and put the diadem on her and show her beauty to all the rulers and the nations, because she was beautiful.
And Astin the queen would not listen to come with the eunuchs, and the king was grieved and enraged.
And he said to his friends, Thus Astin has spoken. So make law and judgment concerning this.
And Arkesaios and Sarsathaios and Malēsear approached him, rulers of Persians and Medes, those near the king, first seated beside the king,
and they reported to him according to the laws what ought to be done to Astin the queen, because she did not do what was commanded by the king through the eunuchs.
And Mouchaios said to the king and the rulers, Not against the king only did Astin the queen do wrong, but also against all the rulers and leaders of the king.
For he recounted to them words of the queen and how she contradicted the king, even as she contradicted King Artaxerxes.
Thus today the remaining princesses of rulers of Persia and Media, hearing what she said to the king, will likewise dare to dishonor their husbands.

If then it seems good to the king, let him issue a royal command and let it be written among laws of Medes and Persians and not otherwise used, that the queen enter to him no more, and let the king give her royal place to a woman better than she.
And let the law which the king makes be heard in his kingdom, and thus all women will give honor to their husbands, from poor to rich.
And the word pleased the king and the rulers, and the king did as Mouchaios spoke.
And he sent into all the kingdom, province by province in their own language, so that there might be fear in their houses.
And after these words the king ceased from wrath and no longer remembered Astin, remembering what she said and how he condemned her.
And servants of the king said, Let incorrupt young girls, beautiful in appearance, be sought for the king.

And let the king appoint local rulers in all provinces of his kingdom, and let them choose virgin girls, beautiful in appearance, into Sousa the city, into the women's house, and let them be delivered to eunuch of the king, keeper of the women, and let cosmetics and the rest of care be given.
And the woman who pleases the king shall reign instead of Astin. And the matter pleased the king, and he did thus.
And there was a Ioudaios man in Sousa the city, and his name was Mardochaios son of Iair, son of Semei, son of Kisaios, from tribe of Beniamin,
who was a captive from Ierousalem, whom Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon carried away captive.

And he had a foster-child, daughter of Aminadab his father's brother, and her name was Esther. And after her parents died he trained her for himself as a wife, and the girl was beautiful in appearance.
And when command of the king was heard, many girls were gathered into Sousa the city under hand of Gai, and Esther was led to Gai, keeper of the women.

And the girl pleased him and found favor before him, and he hurried to give her the cosmetics and the portion and the seven girls appointed to her from the royal house, and he treated her and her maidservants well in the women's house.
And Esther did not reveal her race or her homeland, for Mardochaios commanded her not to report it.
And every day Mardochaios walked around the women's court, looking to see what would happen to Esther.

And this was the time for a girl to go in to the king, when she completed twelve months, for thus the days of treatment are completed: six months being anointed with oil of myrrh and six months with spices and with the women's cosmetics.
And then she goes in to the king, and whatever she says will be given to her to go in with her from the women's house as far as the royal rooms.
In evening she goes in, and by day she returns to the second women's house, where Gai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, is, and she no longer goes in to the king unless called by name.

And when time of Esther, daughter of Aminadab the father's brother of Mardochaios, was fulfilled to go in to the king, she rejected nothing of what Gai the eunuch, keeper of the women, commanded her. For Esther was finding favor from all seeing her.
And Esther went in to Artaxerxes the king in the twelfth month, which is Adar, in seventh year of his reign.
And the king loved Esther, and she found favor beyond all the virgins, and he put upon her the woman's diadem.
And the king made a feast for all his friends and the forces for seven days, and exalted wedding of Esther and made a remission for those under his kingdom.
And Mardochaios was serving in the court.
And Esther did not reveal her homeland, for thus Mardochaios commanded her to fear God and do his commandments, just as when she was with him, and Esther did not change her conduct.
And the two eunuchs of the king, chief bodyguards, were grieved because Mardochaios had been promoted, and they sought to kill Artaxerxes the king.
And the matter became known to Mardochaios, and he signaled it to Esther, and she made known to the king the details of the plot.
And the king examined the two eunuchs and hanged them, and the king ordered it to be recorded for remembrance in the royal library concerning favor of Mardochaios, with praise.
And after these things King Artaxerxes honored Aman son of Amadathos the Bougaian and exalted him and gave him first rank beyond all his friends.
And all in the court were bowing to him, for thus the king commanded it to be done, but Mardochaios was not bowing to him.
And those in the court of the king said to Mardochaios, Mardochaios, why do you disregard things spoken by the king?
Every day they spoke to him, and he was not listening to them, and they reported Mardochaios to Aman, as one opposing words of the king, and Mardochaios showed them that he is a Ioudaios.
And Aman, perceiving that Mardochaios was not bowing to him, was enraged greatly.
And he planned to destroy all the Ioudaioi under kingdom of Artaxerxes.

And he made a decree in twelfth year of reign of Artaxerxes and cast lots, day by day and month by month, so as to destroy race of Mardochaios in one day, and the lot fell on fourteenth of the month, which is Adar.

And he spoke to King Artaxerxes, saying, There is a nation scattered among the nations in all your kingdom, and their laws differ from all nations, and they disregard laws of the king, and it is not advantageous for the king to let them remain.
If it seems good to the king, let it be decreed to destroy them, and I will write ten thousand talents of silver into treasury of the king.
And the king removed the ring and gave it into hand of Aman to seal against the writings against the Ioudaioi.
And the king said to Aman, Keep the silver, and use the nation as you wish.

And scribes of the king were called on thirteenth of the first month, and they wrote as Aman commanded to the generals and the rulers over every province, from India to Ethiopia, to the one hundred twenty-seven provinces, and to rulers of the nations in their own language, by Artaxerxes the king.
And it was sent by book-carriers into kingdom of Artaxerxes to destroy race of the Ioudaioi in one day of the twelfth month, which is Adar, and to plunder their goods.
Copies of the letters were posted province by province, and command was given to all the nations to be ready for this day.
And the matter was hurried, even in Sousa. But the king and Aman were drinking, while the city was troubled.

And Mardochaios, perceiving what was being carried out, tore his garments and put on sackcloth and sprinkled himself with ashes, and leaping through broad place of the city he cried with a loud voice, A nation that did no wrong is being taken away.
And he came as far as the king's gate and stood, for it was not lawful for him to enter the court wearing sackcloth and ashes.
And in every province where the letters were posted, there was cry and beating and great mourning for the Ioudaioi. They spread sackcloth and ashes for themselves.

And maidservants and eunuchs of the queen came in and reported to her, and hearing what happened she was troubled, and she sent to clothe Mardochaios and take away the sackcloth from him, but he was not persuaded.
And Esther called Achrathaios her eunuch, who stood by her, and sent to learn from Mardochaios the exact truth.
And Mardochaios showed him what had happened and the promise which Aman promised to the king, ten thousand talents to the treasury, so as to destroy the Ioudaioi.

And he gave him copy of the notice posted in Sousa for their destruction, to show Esther, and he told him to command her, after going in, to plead with the king and urge him for the people, remembering days of your humiliation, how you were nourished in my hand, because Aman, the second to the kingdom, has spoken against us for death. Call upon the Lord and speak to the king concerning us and rescue us from death.
And Achrathaios went in and spoke to her all these words.
And Esther said to Achrathaios, Go to Mardochaios and say that

all nations of the kingdom know that every man or woman who enters to the king in the inner court uncalled has no salvation, except the one to whom the king stretches out the golden scepter, that one will be saved. And I have not been called to go in to the king these thirty days.
And Achrathaios reported to Mardochaios all words of Esther.
And Mardochaios said to Achrathaios, Go and tell Esther, Do not say to yourself that you alone in the kingdom will be saved beyond all the Ioudaioi.

For if you disregard in this time, help and shelter will be for the Ioudaioi from another place, but you and house of your father will perish. And who knows whether for this very time you came to reign?
And Esther sent back the one who came to her, to Mardochaios, saying,

Go, gather the Ioudaioi in Sousa and fast for me, and do not eat or drink for three days, night and day. And I and my maidservants will likewise go without food, and then I will go in to the king contrary to the law. If then I must perish, I will perish.
And Mardochaios went and did all that Esther commanded him.
And it happened on the third day, when she ceased praying, she took off garments of service and put on her glory.
And after lifting the golden scepter she placed it on her neck and kissed it and said, Speak to me.
And the king said, What do you want, Esther, and what is your request? Even to half of my kingdom, it shall be yours.
And Esther said, My marked day is today. If then it seems good to the king, let him and Aman come to the feast which I will make today.
And the king said, Hasten Aman, so that we may do word of Esther. And both came to the feast which Esther spoke of.
And during the drinking the king said to Esther, What is it, Queen Esther? It shall be yours, whatever you ask.
And she said, My petition and my request are this:
If I found favor before the king, let the king and Aman come tomorrow to the feast which I will make for them, and tomorrow I will do the same things.
And Aman went out from the king overjoyed and rejoicing. But when Aman saw Mardochaios the Ioudaios in the court, he was enraged greatly.
And after entering his own house he called his friends and Zōsara his wife.
And he showed them his wealth and the honor which the king placed on him and how he made him hold first place and lead the kingdom.
And Aman said, The queen called no one to the feast with the king except me, and for tomorrow I have been called.
And these things do not please me whenever I see Mardochaios the Ioudaios in the court.

And Zōsara his wife and the friends said to him, Let a timber of fifty cubits be cut for you, and in the morning speak to the king, and let Mardochaios be hanged on the timber. But you go into the feast with the king and rejoice. And the word pleased Aman, and the timber was prepared.
But the Lord drove sleep away from the king in that night, and he told his teacher to bring in memorial records of the days, to read to him.
And he found the writings written concerning Mardochaios, how he reported to the king about the two eunuchs of the king while they were guarding him and seeking to lay hands on Artaxerxes.
And the king said, What honor or favor have we done for Mardochaios? And the servants of the king said, You did nothing for him.

And as the king was inquiring concerning favor of Mardochaios, behold Aman was in the court. And the king said, Who is in the court? And Aman came in to speak to the king to hang Mardochaios on the timber which he prepared.
And servants of the king said, Behold, Aman stands in the court. And the king said, Call him.
And the king said to Aman, What shall I do for the man whom I wish to honor? And Aman said in himself, Whom does the king wish to honor except me?
And he said to the king, For the man whom the king wishes to honor,
let servants of the king bring linen robe which the king wears and horse on which the king rides,

and let one of the king's glorious friends give it, and let him robe the man whom the king loves and lift him upon the horse and proclaim through broad place of the city, saying, Thus it shall be to every man whom the king honors.
And the king said to Aman, As you spoke, so do to Mardochaios the Ioudaios, who serves in the court, and let not one word of what you spoke fall away.

And Aman took the robe and the horse and robed Mardochaios and lifted him upon the horse and went through broad place of the city and proclaimed, saying, Thus it shall be to every man whom the king wishes to honor.
And Mardochaios returned to the court, but Aman returned to his own house grieving, with head covered.

And Aman recounted to Zōsara his wife and to the friends what happened to him, and the friends and the wife said to him, If Mardochaios is from race of Ioudaioi, you began to be humbled before him, and falling you will fall; you will never be able to resist him, because living God is with him.
While they were still speaking, the eunuchs arrived, hurrying Aman to the drinking-feast which Esther prepared.
And the king and Aman went in to drink with the queen.
And on the second day during the drinking the king said, What is it, Queen Esther, and what is your petition and what is your request? Even to half of my kingdom, let it be yours.
And she answered and said, If I found favor before the king, let my life be given for my petition and my people for my request.

For I and my people were sold for destruction and plundering and slavery, we and our children, for boy-servants and girl-servants. And I kept silent, for the accuser is not worthy of the king's court.
And the king said, Who is this one who dared to do this thing?
And Esther said, An enemy, Aman, this evil one. And Aman was thrown into turmoil before the king and the queen.
And the king rose from the banquet into the garden, but Aman was begging the queen, for he saw himself in evils.

And the king returned from the garden. Aman had fallen on the couch, begging the queen. And the king said, So then will he even force the woman in my own house? And Aman, hearing, was struck in the face.

And Bouthathan, one of the eunuchs, said to the king, Behold, Aman also prepared a timber for Mardochaios, the one who spoke for the king, and it stands in Aman's house, fifty cubits. And the king said, Let him be impaled on it.
And Aman was hanged on the timber which he prepared for Mardochaios, and then the king ceased from wrath.
And on that day King Artaxerxes gave to Esther all things that belonged to Aman the accuser, and Mardochaios was called by the king, for Esther showed that he was related to her.
And the king took the ring which he removed from Aman and gave it to Mardochaios, and Esther appointed Mardochaios over all things of Aman.
And Esther added and spoke to the king and fell at his feet and asked him to remove evil of Aman and all he did against the Ioudaioi.
And the king stretched out to Esther the golden scepter. And Esther rose to stand by the king.
And Esther said, If it seems good to you and I found favor, let the letters sent by Aman be turned back, the ones written to destroy the Ioudaioi who are in your kingdom.
For how shall I be able to see mistreatment of my people? And how shall I be saved amid destruction of my homeland?
And the king said to Esther, If all things of Aman I gave and granted to you, and him I hanged on timber because he laid hands on the Ioudaioi, what do you still seek?
Write also yourselves in my name as seems good to you, and seal it with my ring. For whatever is written when the king commands and sealed with my ring, there is no contradicting it.

And the scribes were called in the first month, which is Nisan, on the twenty-third of that year, and it was written for the Ioudaioi what he commanded to the administrators and rulers of the satrapies, from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven satrapies, province by province in its own language.
And it was written through the king and sealed with his ring, and they sent the letters through book-carriers,
just as he commanded them to use their laws in every city, to help themselves and deal with their adversaries and those opposing them as they wish,
on one day in all kingdom of Artaxerxes, on thirteenth of the twelfth month, which is Adar.
And let copies be publicly posted in all the kingdom, and let all the Ioudaioi be ready for this day to fight those set against them.
So the riders went out hurrying to fulfill what the king spoke, and the decree was also posted in Sousa.
And Mardochaios went out clothed in royal robe and wearing golden crown and linen purple diadem, and those in Sousa, seeing, rejoiced.
And for the Ioudaioi there came light and gladness,

in city and province wherever the decree and notice were posted, joy and gladness came for the Ioudaioi, a feast and rejoicing, and many of the nations were circumcised and became Ioudaizing because of fear of the Ioudaioi.
For in the twelfth month, on thirteenth of the month, which is Adar, the letters written by the king were at hand.
On that day those opposing the Ioudaioi were destroyed, for no one stood against them, fearing them.
For rulers of the satrapies and the tyrants and the king's scribes were honoring the Ioudaioi, for fear of Mardochaios was pressing upon them.
For decree of the king had fallen that his name be spoken in all the kingdom.
And in Sousa the city the Ioudaioi killed five hundred men,
both Pharsannestain and Delphōn and Phasga,
and Phardatha and Barea and Sarbacha,
and Marmasima and Arouphaios and Arsaios and Zabouthaithan,
the ten sons of Aman son of Amadathos the Bougaian, enemy of the Ioudaioi, and they plundered.
On that day the number of the slain in Sousa was reported to the king.
And the king said to Esther, The Ioudaioi destroyed five hundred men in Sousa the city, and in the district how do you think they acted? What more do you request? And it shall be yours.
And Esther said to the king, Let it be given to the Ioudaioi to act likewise tomorrow, and to hang the ten sons of Aman.
And he permitted it to happen thus and ordered bodies of Aman's sons to be hung for the Ioudaioi of the city.
And the Ioudaioi were gathered in Sousa on the fourteenth of Adar and killed three hundred men, and they plundered nothing.

And the rest of the Ioudaioi in the kingdom gathered and were helping themselves, and they rested from the war. For they destroyed fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth of Adar and plundered nothing.
And they rested on the fourteenth of the same month and kept it as day of rest with joy and gladness.
But the Ioudaioi in Sousa the city were gathered on the fourteenth and did not rest, but kept the fifteenth with joy and gladness.

Therefore the Ioudaioi scattered in every country outside keep the fourteenth of Adar as a good day with joy, sending portions each to his neighbor, and those dwelling in the capitals keep also the fifteenth of Adar as a good day of rejoicing, sending portions to neighbors.
And Mardochaios wrote these words into a book and sent to the Ioudaioi, as many as were in kingdom of Artaxerxes, both near and far,
to establish these good days, to keep both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,

for in these days the Ioudaioi rested from their enemies, and the month in which, being Adar, it was turned for them from mourning into joy and from grief into a good day, to keep all as good days of marriages and rejoicing, sending portions to friends and to the poor.
And the Ioudaioi accepted it, just as Mardochaios wrote to them,
how Aman son of Amadathos the Macedonian warred against them, as he made decree and lot to destroy them,
and how he entered to the king, saying to hang Mardochaios. But the evils which he attempted to bring upon the Ioudaioi came upon him, and he and his children were hanged.

Therefore these days were called Phrourai because of the lots, for in their language they call them Phrourai, because of words of this letter and what they suffered because of these things and what happened to them.

And the Ioudaioi established and accepted it upon themselves and upon their seed and upon those added to them, and they will use no other way, but these days will be a memorial kept generation by generation and city and father-house and province.
And these days of Phrourai will be kept for all time, and their memorial shall never fail from the generations.
And Esther the queen, daughter of Aminadab, and Mardochaios the Ioudaios wrote all that they did, even the confirming of the letter of Phrourai.
And Mardochaios and Esther the queen established for themselves by themselves, and then after establishing according to their safety and their counsel,
Esther established by word forever, and it was written for remembrance.
And the king wrote taxes upon the kingdom of both land and sea.
And his strength and bravery and the wealth and glory of his kingdom, behold, these are written in book of kings of Persia and Media for remembrance.
And Mardochaios succeeded King Artaxerxes and was great in the kingdom and glorified by the Ioudaioi and loved, recounting the way of life to all his nation.
There was a certain man in the land of Ausitis, whose name was Iōb, and that man was true, blameless, righteous, god-fearing, turning away from every evil thing.
And there came to him seven sons and three daughters.

And his livestock was seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred grazing she-donkeys, and very much service, and great works were his upon the land. And that man was noblest of those from sunrise.
And his sons, going to one another, were making a feast each day, bringing along also their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

And when days of the feast were completed, Iōb sent and purified them. Rising early, he offered sacrifices for them according to their number, and one calf for sin concerning their souls. For Iōb said, Lest my sons thought evil things in their mind toward God. Thus Iōb was doing all the days.
And when this day came, behold, angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the slanderer came with them.
And the Lord said to the slanderer, From where are you here? And answering, the slanderer said to the Lord, After going around the earth and walking about under heaven, I am here.
And the Lord said to him, Did you set your mind against my servant Iōb, because there is no man like him on the earth, blameless, true, god-fearing, turning away from every evil thing?
And the slanderer answered and said before the Lord, Does Iōb fear God for nothing?
Did you not fence in things outside him and inside his house and outside all that belongs to him round about? Works of his hands you blessed, and his cattle you made many upon the earth.
But stretch out your hand and touch all that he has, and surely he will bless you to your face.
Then the Lord said to the slanderer, Behold, all things that are his I give into your hand, only do not touch him. And the slanderer went out from the Lord.
And it happened on a day when Iōb's sons and daughters were drinking wine in house of their elder brother,
and behold, a messenger came to Iōb and said to him, The yoke of oxen were plowing, and the she-donkeys were grazing beside them,
and the raiders came and took them captive, and the servants they killed with swords. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Iōb, Fire fell from heaven and burned up the sheep and devoured the shepherds likewise. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.

While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Iōb, The horsemen made against us three heads, and they surrounded the camels and took them captive, and the servants they killed with swords. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.
While this one was still speaking, another messenger came, saying to Iōb, Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking at their elder brother's house,
and suddenly a great wind came from the wilderness and touched the four corners of the house, and the house fell on your children, and they died. And I alone escaped and came to report to you.
So Iōb rose, tore his garments, shaved hair of his head, and falling to the ground worshiped and said,
Naked I came out from womb of my mother, naked also I will go away there. The Lord gave, the Lord took away. As it seemed good to the Lord, so also it came to pass. Let name of the Lord be blessed.
In all these things that happened to him, Iōb sinned in nothing before the Lord and gave no folly to God.
And it came to be on this day also that angels of God came to stand before the Lord, and the slanderer came among them to stand before the Lord.
And the Lord said to the slanderer, From where do you come? Then the slanderer said before the Lord, After passing through what is under heaven and walking all around, I am here.

And the Lord said to the slanderer, Did you then give attention to my servant Iōb, because there is no man like him on the earth, innocent, true, blameless, god-fearing, turning away from every evil, and he still holds fast his innocence? Yet you spoke against his possessions to destroy them for nothing.
And taking up the matter, the slanderer said to the Lord, Skin for skin, all things a man has he will pay for his life.
But stretch out your hand and touch his bones and his flesh, and surely he will bless you to your face.
And the Lord said to the slanderer, Behold, I hand him over to you; only preserve his life.
And the slanderer went out from the Lord and struck Iōb with a grievous sore from feet to head.
And he took a potsherd to scrape the discharge, and he sat upon the dung-heap outside the city.

And when much time had passed, his wife said to him, How long will you endure, saying, Behold, I wait yet a little time, expecting hope of my deliverance? For behold, your memorial has vanished from the earth, sons and daughters of my womb, pangs and labors which I toiled for in vain with hardships. And you yourself sit in decay of worms, passing the night in the open air. And I am a wanderer and servant, going from place to place and house to house, waiting for sun to set so that I may rest from labors and pains that now hold me fast. But speak some word to the Lord and die.

And looking at her, he said to her, You spoke like one of the foolish women. If we accepted good things from hand of the Lord, shall we not bear evil things? In all these things that happened to him, Iōb sinned in nothing with his lips before God.

And hearing all the evils that came upon him, his three friends came, each from his own country, to him: Eliphas the Thaimanite king, Baldad the Sauchaian tyrant, and Sophar the Minaian king. And they came to him with one purpose, to encourage and visit him.
And seeing him from far off, they did not recognize him, and crying with a loud voice they wept, each tearing his own robe and scattering dust.
They sat with him seven days and seven nights, and none of them spoke, for they saw that the blow was dreadful and very great.
After this Iōb opened his mouth
and cursed his day, saying,
Let the day perish in which I was born, and the night in which they said, Behold, a male.
Let that day be darkness, and let not the Lord seek it from above, nor let light come upon it.
Let darkness and shadow of death take it. Let gloom come upon it.
Let the day and that night be cursed. Let darkness take it away. Let it not be among days of the year, nor counted among days of months.
But let that night be pain, and let no gladness come upon it, nor joy.
But let the one cursing that day curse it, the one preparing to master the great sea-beast.
Let stars of that night be darkened. Let it wait and not come into light, nor see morning-star rising,
because it did not shut gates of my mother's womb, for then it would have removed pain from my eyes.
For why did I not die in the belly? And coming out from the womb, why did I not immediately perish?
Why then did knees meet me? And why breasts, that I sucked?
Now, having lain down, I would have been quiet. Having slept, I would have rested
with kings, counselors of earth, who gloried themselves over swords,
or with rulers whose gold was much, who filled their houses with silver,
or like miscarriage coming out from womb of a mother, or like infants who never saw light.
There the ungodly burned out rage of wrath. There the weary in body rested.
And there the eternal ones together did not hear voice of tax-collector.
Small and great are there, and servant not fearing his lord.
Why then is light given to those in bitterness, and life to souls in pains,
who long for death and do not obtain it, digging for it as for treasures,
who become overjoyed if they should attain it?
Death is rest to a man, for God shut in against him.
For before my food, groaning comes to me, and I weep, being held fast by fear.
For fear which I pondered came upon me, and what I dreaded met me.
I neither had peace nor was quiet nor rested, but wrath came to me.
And taking up the matter, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,
Were many times spoken to you in distress? But strength of your words, who will bear?
For you instructed many and encouraged weak hands.
And those failing you raised up by words, and upon knees without strength you put courage.
But now pain comes upon you and touches you, and you were hasty.
Is not your fear foolishness, and your hope, and innocence of your way?
Remember then, who being pure perished? Or when did true men perish root and all?
In the way I saw, those plowing improper things and those sowing them will reap pains for themselves.
By command of the Lord they will perish, and by breath of his wrath they will be wiped out.
Strength of lion, voice of lioness, and boast of dragons were quenched.
Ant-lion perished for not having food, and lion cubs abandoned one another.
But if any true word happened in your sayings, none of these evils would ever have met you. Will not my ear receive strange things from him?
But fears and sound of night, fear falling on men,
dread met me and trembling, and greatly my bones shook together.
And a spirit came upon my face, and my hairs and flesh shuddered.
I stood up and did not recognize; I looked, and there was no form before my eyes, but only a breeze, and I was hearing a voice:
What then? Shall mortal be pure before the Lord, or shall a man be blameless by his works?
If he does not trust in his servants, and against his angels he devised something crooked,
then those dwelling in houses of clay, from which we also are from the same clay, he struck like a moth.
And from morning until evening they no longer exist, because they were not able to help themselves. They perished.
For he breathed on them and they dried up. They perished for not having wisdom.
But call, if anyone will hear you, or if you will see any of the holy angels.
For anger kills the fool, and jealousy kills the wandering one.
But I saw fools throwing down root, yet immediately their way of life was eaten up.
Let their sons be far from deliverance, and let them be beaten at doors of inferiors, and there will be no one rescuing.
For what they gathered, righteous men will eat, but they themselves will not be delivered from evils. Let their strength be drained away.
For toil will not come out from the earth, nor will pain sprout up from the mountains.
But man is born for toil, and young vultures fly to the heights.
Yet I will petition the Lord, and I will call on the Master of all.
He does great and unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things beyond number,
giving rain upon the earth, sending water upon what is under heaven,
making lowly ones into height, raising up those who were lost,
turning aside counsels of the crafty, and their hands will never do what is true,
the one catching wise men in their cunning, and overthrowing counsel of the twisted,
in daytime darkness will meet them, and at noon they will grope as in night.
But let the weak perish in war, and let the powerless come out from hand of the mighty.
And let there be hope for the powerless, but mouth of the unrighteous be stopped.
But blessed is man whom the Lord corrected; do not reject discipline of the Almighty.
For he causes pain and again restores. He struck, and his hands healed.
Six times from necessities he will deliver you, and in the seventh evil will not touch you.
In famine he will rescue you from death, and in war he will free you from hand of iron.
From scourge of the tongue he will hide you, and you will not fear evils coming.
You will laugh at unjust and lawless men, and you will not fear from wild beasts,
for wild beasts will be at peace with you.
Then you will know that your house will be at peace, and dwelling of your tent will never go wrong.
And you will know that your seed is many, and your children will be like all-herbage of the field.
And you will come to the grave like ripe grain harvested in its season, or like heap of threshing floor gathered at its time.
Behold, these things we searched out. These are what we heard. But you, know for yourself if you did anything.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
If only someone might weigh my anger, and lift my pains together in balance.
For now it would be heavier than sand of seashore; but, as it seems, my words are worthless.
For arrows of Lord are in my body, whose fury drinks up my blood; whenever I begin to speak, they stab me.
For surely wild donkey does not cry for nothing, unless seeking grain; nor will ox bellow at manger while having fodder.
Will bread be eaten without salt? Or is there taste in empty words?
For my soul cannot cease, for I see my foods as stench, like smell of lion.
If only my request might come, and Lord might give my hope.
Let Lord begin and wound me; but in end let him not destroy me.
Let my city be grave, upon whose walls I leaped; upon it I will by no means spare myself, for I did not lie about words of holy God.
For what strength have I, that I keep enduring? Or what time remains for me, that my soul keeps bearing?
Is my strength strength of stones, or is my flesh bronze?
Or was I not trusting in him? But help has gone far from me.
Mercy renounced me, and visitation of Lord overlooked me.
My near ones did not regard me; like failing torrents, or like wave they passed me by.
Those who feared me before have now fallen upon me, like snow or frozen ice.
As things melted when heat came, what they were was not recognized.
Thus I too was abandoned by all; I perished and became homeless.
Look at ways of Thaimanites, paths of Sabaeans, those who look intently.
They will owe shame, those trusting in cities and riches.
But now you too fell upon me without mercy, so that seeing my wound you were afraid.
For what? Did I ask anything from you, or do I need some of your strength?
So as to save me from enemies, or rescue me from hand of rulers?
Teach me, and I will be silent; if I have gone astray, show me.
As it seems, words of truth are worthless, for I do not ask strength from you.
Nor will your reproof stop me with words, for neither will I endure sound of your speech.
Only because you fall upon orphan, and spring against your friend.
But now, looking into your faces, I will not lie.
Sit down then, and let there not be injustice; and again come together with righteous judgment.
For there is no injustice on my tongue; does not my throat ponder understanding?
Is not life of man on earth a trial, and his life like that of day-laborer?
Like servant fearing his master and having attained shade, like hired man waiting for his wage,
so I too inherited empty months, and nights of pains were given me.
If I lie down, I say, When day? and when I rise again, When evening? And I am full of pains from evening until morning.
My body is mixed with rottenness of worms; I melt clods of earth, scraping off the discharge.
My life is lighter than speech, and has perished in empty hope.
Remember then that my life is breath, and my eye will no longer return to see good.
Eye of one seeing me will not look on me; your eyes are on me, and I am no longer.
Like cloud cleansed away from heaven, if man goes down to Hades, he will certainly not come up again.
Nor will he ever return again to his own house, nor will his place know him anymore.
But therefore neither will I spare my mouth; I will speak in distress, opening bitterness of my soul while hard pressed.
Am I sea or dragon, that you set a guard over me?
If I say, My bed will comfort me, and my couch will bear my complaint for me,
then you frighten me with dreams and terrify me with visions.
You will free my soul from breath, and my bones from death.
For I will not live forever, that I should be patient. Depart from me, for my life is empty.
What is man, that you magnified him, or that you set your mind on him,
or make visitation of him until morning, and judge him for rest?
Until when will you not let me be, nor release me until I swallow my spittle in pain?
If I sinned, what can I do to you, knower of minds of men? Why did you set me as your accuser? And I have become burden to you.
And why did you not make forgetfulness of my lawlessness and cleansing of my sin? For now I will depart into earth, and seeking me early, I am no more.
And taking up the matter, Baldad the Sauchite says,
How long will you speak these things, wind of many words from your mouth?
Will Lord do injustice in judging, or will maker of all disturb what is right?
If your sons sinned before him, he sent them away in hand of their lawlessness.
But you, rise early toward Lord, begging Almighty.
If you are pure and true, he will hear your petition and restore to you dwelling of righteousness.
Then your first things will be few, but your last things beyond counting.
Ask indeed former generation, and search out race of fathers.
For we are of yesterday and do not know; for our life on earth is shadow.
Will not these teach you and tell you, and bring out words from their heart?
Does papyrus flourish without water, or will reed rise high without drink?
While still on its root and not yet cut, before any herb drinks, does it not dry up?
So then will be end of all who forget Lord, for hope of ungodly will perish.
For his house will be uninhabited, and his tent will turn out to be spider's web.
If he lean on his house, it will not stand; if he take hold of it, it will not endure.
For it is moist under sun, and from its decay its shoot will come out.
It sleeps upon gathering of stones, and in midst of pebbles it will live.
If place swallow it up, it will deny it: You have not seen such things.
For such is overthrow of ungodly, and from earth another will sprout.
For Lord will by no means reject blameless one, but will not receive any gift of ungodly.
