Yet he will fill mouth of true ones with laughter, and their lips with confession.
But their enemies will clothe themselves with shame, and dwelling of ungodly will not be.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
In truth I know that it is so; for how will a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
If he should wish to enter judgment with him, he will not answer him one word out of thousand.
For he is wise in mind, mighty and great. Who, having hardened himself against him, endured?
He who ages mountains, and they do not know, overthrowing them in anger.
He who shakes what is under heaven from foundations, and its pillars totter.
He who says to sun, and it does not rise, and seals up stars.
He who stretched out heaven alone and walks as upon ground on sea.
He who makes Pleiad and Evening Star and Bear and chambers of south.
He who does great and unsearchable things, glorious and astonishing things without number.
If he pass over me, I will not see; if he go by me, I would not know.
If someone turn him away, who will turn him back? Or who will say to him, What have you done?
For he turned away wrath; under him sea-monsters beneath heaven were bowed down.
And if he should hear me, will he discern my words?
For even if I am righteous, he will not hear me; I will plead with my judge.
And if I call and he answers, I do not believe that he has heard my voice.
Let him not rub me out in storm-cloud; he made my shatterings many for nothing.
For he does not let me take breath, but filled me with bitterness.
If it is matter of strength, he is strong; but in judgment, who will withstand him?
Even if I am righteous, my mouth will act ungodly; if I am blameless, I will turn crooked.
For even if I did act ungodly, I do not know in my soul; only this, that my life is taken away.
Therefore I said, wrath destroys both great man and ruler.
For worthless men are remarkable in death, but righteous are laughed to scorn.
For earth is given into hands of ungodly; he covers faces of its judges. But if not he, who is it?
My life is lighter than runner; they fled and did not know.
Or is there track of way for ships, or of eagle flying and seeking food?
If then I say, I will forget my speaking, stooping with face I will groan,
I shudder in all my limbs, for I know that you will not leave me innocent.
Since I am ungodly, why then did I not die?
For if I wash myself with snow and cleanse my hands with purity,
sufficiently you dipped me in filth, and my garment loathed me.
For you are not man like me, against whom I will answer, that we might come together into judgment.
If only there were mediator of us, and reprover, and one hearing between both.
Let him take his rod away from me, and let his fear not whirl me about.
Then I would not fear, but speak, for I do not know myself so.
Weary in my soul, groaning, I will let my words go upon him; I will speak bitterness of my soul while hard pressed.
And I will say to Lord, Do not treat me as ungodly; teach me why you judged me thus.
Is it good to you if I act unjustly, that you reject works of your hands, but give heed to counsel of ungodly?
Do you look as mortal looks, or see as man sees?
Is your life human, or your years those of man,
that you searched out my lawlessness and tracked down my sins?
For you know that I did not act ungodly, but there is none rescuing from your hands.
Your hands formed me and made me; then changing, you struck me.
Remember that you molded me like clay, and you turn me back into earth.
Did you not milk me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
With skin and flesh you clothed me, and with bones and sinews you wove me.
Life and mercy you set with me, and your oversight guarded my spirit.
Holding these things within yourself, I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible to you.
If I sin, you watch me, and from lawlessness you did not make me innocent.
If I am ungodly, woe to me; if I am righteous, I cannot lift myself up, for I am full of dishonor.
For I am hunted like lion for slaughter, and again changing, you destroy me terribly.
Renewing my examination against me, you used great wrath toward me and brought trials upon me.
Why then did you bring me out from womb? Would that I had died and eye had not seen me.
And I would have become as if I had not been. Why then was I not carried from belly to grave?
Is not time of my life small? Let me be, that I may rest a little,
before I go from where I will not return, into land dark and gloomy,
into land of eternal darkness, where there is no light, nor seeing of life among mortals.
And taking up the matter, Sophar the Minaian says,
Will one who says many things also answer back? Or does wordy man think himself righteous, blessed though born of woman and short-lived?
Do not become abundant in words, for there is no one answering you.
For do not say, I am pure in works and blameless before him.
But how might Lord speak to you and open his lips with you!
Then he would declare to you power of wisdom, because they will be double to what is with you. And then you will know that what came to you from Lord matches what you sinned.
Will you find track of Lord, or reach to ends of what Almighty made?
Heaven is high; what will you do? Deeper than things in Hades; what do you know?
Longer than measure of earth and broader than sea.
If he overturn all things, who will say to him, What did you do?
For he knows works of lawless men, and seeing wrongs he will not overlook.
But man drifts vainly in words, and mortal born of woman is like desert donkey.
For if you set your heart pure and stretch out hands toward him,
if any lawless thing is in your hands, put it far from you, and let not injustice lodge in your dwelling.
For then your face will shine like pure water, and you will strip off filth and by no means fear.
And you will forget toil, like wave that passed by, and you will not be alarmed.
And your prayer will be like morning star, and life will rise for you from midday.
And you will be confident because there is hope for you; and out of care and anxiety peace will appear for you.
For you will be at rest, and none will make war on you; and many changing course will entreat you.
But salvation will fail them, for their hope is destruction, and eyes of ungodly will melt.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
Then you are men indeed, and wisdom will die with you?
But I too have heart like you.
For righteous and blameless man became object of mockery.
For appointed time was prepared for him to fall under others and for his houses to be plundered by lawless men.
Yet let no one, being evil, trust that he will be innocent; all who provoke Lord, is there not examination for them too?
But now ask beasts, if they will tell you, and birds of heaven, if they will report to you.
Or tell earth, if it should explain to you, and fish of sea will recount to you.
Who does not know in all these that hand of Lord made these things,
if not that in his hand is soul of every living thing and breath of every human?
For throat discerns words, and palate tastes foods.
In much time is wisdom, and in long life knowledge.
With him are wisdom and power; with him counsel and understanding.
If he throws down, who will build? If he shuts against men, who will open?
If he hold back water, he will dry earth; if he let it loose, he ruined it by overthrowing.
With him are might and strength; with him knowledge and understanding.
Leading counselors away captive, he drove judges of earth mad.
Setting kings on thrones, he bound belt around their loins.
Sending priests away captive, he overthrew rulers of earth.
Changing lips of faithful men, he takes away understanding of elders.
Pouring dishonor on rulers, but healing humble ones.
Revealing deep things from darkness, and bringing shadow of death into light.
Leading nations astray and destroying them, spreading out nations and guiding them.
Changing hearts of rulers of earth, he led them astray in path they did not know.
Let them grope darkness and not light, and let them wander like drunkard.
Behold, my eye has seen these things, and my ear heard them.
What you know, I also know; I am not less understanding than you.
But indeed I will speak to Lord, and if he wishes I will reason before him.
But you are unjust physicians and healers of evils, all of you.
If only you would be silent, and it would turn out to be wisdom for you.
Hear correction of my mouth, and give attention to judgment of my lips.
Do you not speak before Lord, and utter deceit before him?
Will you shrink back, and become judges yourselves?
It will indeed be good if he searches you out, if in doing all things you attach yourselves to him?
Yet he will surely reprove you, even if in secret you admire faces.
Will not his terrors whirl you, and fear from him fall upon you?
Your boasting will turn out equal to ashes, and body to clay.
Be silent, so I may speak, and let wrath rest from me.
Taking my flesh in my teeth, I will put my soul in my hand.
If Mighty One should lay hand on me, since he has begun, yet I will speak and reason before him.
And this will turn out for me into salvation, for deceit will not enter before him.
Hear, hear my words, for I will declare with you listening.
Behold, I am near my judgment; I know that I will appear righteous.
For who is he that will contend with me? Then I would be silent and expire.
But use two things toward me; then I will not hide from your face.
Hold back your hand from me, and let not your fear terrify me.
Then you will call, and I will answer you; or you will speak, and I will give you reply.
How many are my sins and lawless acts? Teach me what they are.
Why do you hide from me and count me your opponent?
Will you fear leaf moved by wind, or oppose me as grass carried by breath?
For you wrote bitter things against me and laid on me sins of youth.
You put my foot in restraint, and watched all my works, and came up to roots of my feet.
And I grow old like skin-bag, like garment eaten by moth.
Mortal born of woman, short-lived and full of wrath.
Like flower blooming he fell off; he fled like shadow and will not stand.
And on this one you made account, and this one you caused to enter judgment before you?
For who will be clean from defilement? No one.
Even if his life is one day on earth, and his months beyond number are with you, you set him a time and he will not pass it.
Depart from him, that he may rest and take pleasure in his life like hired man.
For there is hope for tree: if it be cut down, it will bloom again, and its shoot will not fail.
If its root should grow old in earth and its stump die in rock,
by scent of water it will blossom and make harvest like young plant.
But man, having died, is gone; and mortal, having fallen, is no more.
For in time sea grows scarce, and river, having deserted, dried up.
So man, having fallen asleep, will certainly not rise until heaven is stitched together. They will not be awakened from their sleep.
If only you had kept me in Hades and hidden me until your wrath ceased, and set me a time in which you would remember me.
For if man die, will he live again? Having completed days of my life, I wait until I become again.
Then you will call, and I will listen to you. Do not reject works of your hands.
You counted my practices, and none of my sins will escape you.
You sealed my lawless acts in purse, and marked if in anything I transgressed unwillingly.
Yet mountain falling will collapse, and rock will grow old out of its place.
Waters wore stones smooth, and waters flooded dust of earth, and you destroyed hope of man.
Pushing him to end, he is gone; you set his face and sent him away.
If his sons become many, he does not know; if they become few, he is not aware.
But his flesh grieved, and his soul mourned.
And taking up the matter, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,
Will wise man give answer of understanding's spirit, and fill belly with pain?
Reproving with words that are not needed, and speeches with no profit.
Indeed you cast off fear and brought such words to completion before Lord.
You are guilty by words of your mouth, nor did you discern words of mighty men.
Your own mouth will reprove you, not I; your lips will testify against you.
For were you first of men to be born, or were you fixed in place before hills?
Did you hear ordinance of Lord, and did wisdom reach to you alone?
For what do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not also with us?
Both gray-haired and aged men are among us, heavier in days than your father.
For little things in which you sinned you were chastised greatly; you spoke excessively beyond measure.
What did your heart dare, and what did your eyes bring on?
That you burst out wrath against Lord and brought out such words from your mouth.
For what is mortal, that he will be blameless? Or how will one born of woman be righteous?
If he does not trust his holy ones, and heaven is not clean before him,
how much more abominable and unclean is man, drinking injustice like drink.
But I will declare to you; hear me. What things I indeed have seen, I will tell you,
what wise men will say and did not hide from their fathers.
To them alone earth was given, and foreigner did not come upon them.
All life of ungodly is in care, and numbered years are given to tyrant.
Fear is in his ears; when he thinks he is at peace, destruction will come on him.
Let him not believe he will turn back from darkness, for he is already appointed into hands of iron.
He is appointed for vultures as food; he knows in himself that he remains for corpse, and dark day will whirl him.
Necessity and distress will hold him, like commanding general falling in front rank.
Because he raised hands against Lord and stiffened neck against Lord Almighty.
He ran against him in insolence, in thickness of hump of his shield.
Because he covered his face in his fat, and made collar upon thighs.
Let him lodge in deserted cities, and enter uninhabited houses; what those men prepared, others will carry off.
He will by no means grow rich, nor will his possessions remain; his shadow will not fall on earth.
Nor will he escape darkness; wind will wither his shoot, and his flower will fall off.
Let him not believe he endures, for empty things will turn out for him.
His cutting-down will be completed before its time, and his shoot will not flourish.
Let him be harvested like unripe grape before its time, and fall off like flower of olive.
For witness of ungodly is death, and fire will burn houses of gift-takers.
In belly he will receive pains, and empty things will turn out for him, and his belly will bear deceit.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
I heard many such things, all of you comforters of evils.
For is there not order to windy words? Or what troubles you that you answer?
I too would speak like you, if only your soul lay in place of mine; then I would exult over you with words and shake head against you.
But let there be strength in my mouth; I will not spare movement of my lips.
For if I speak, I will not ease the wound; if I keep silent, how much less will I be wounded?
But now he made me worn out, rotten and foolish.
He seized me for witness; it became so, and my lie rose up in me, answering against my face.
Using wrath, he threw me down; he gnashed teeth at me. Arrows of his raiders fell on me.
With sharpness of eyes he leaped on me; he struck me sharply on cheek, and with one accord they rushed upon me.
For Lord handed me over into hands of unjust one, and threw me upon ungodly men.
At peace, he scattered me; taking me by hair he tore me, set me up like target.
Spears encircled me, throwing into my kidneys without sparing; he poured my gall upon earth.
He cast me down corpse upon corpse; mighty ones ran upon me.
I sewed sackcloth upon my skin, and my strength was quenched in earth.
My belly is burned from weeping, and shadow upon my eyelids.
Yet there was nothing unjust in my hands, and my prayer was pure.
Earth, do not cover over blood of my flesh, nor let there be place for my cry.
And now, behold, my witness is in heavens, and my confirmer in highest places.
Let my petition come to Lord, and before him let my eye drop tears.
Let there be reproof for man before Lord, and son of man for his neighbor.
For numbered years have come, and I will go way from which I will not return.
I am ruined, carried by breath; I beg for burial and do not obtain it.
I am worn out in supplication. And what have I done?
Strangers stole my goods. Who is this? Let him be bound with my hand.
For you hid their heart from understanding; because of this you will not exalt them.
He will declare evils for a share, and my eyes melted away over my sons.
And you set me for byword among nations, and I became a laughingstock to them.
For my eyes are dimmed from wrath; I have been greatly besieged by all.
True men were amazed at this, and righteous man would rise up against lawless one.
Let faithful one hold fast his own way, and clean of hands take courage.
But all of you brace yourselves and come; for I do not find truth among you.
My days passed in stench, and joints of my heart were broken.
They turned night into day; light is near from face of darkness.
For if I endure, Hades is my house; in gloom my bed is spread.
I called death my father, and rot my mother and my sister.
Where then is my hope? Or my good things? Will I see them?
Will they go down with me into Hades, or shall we descend together to dust?
And taking up the matter, Baldad the Sauchite says,
How long will you not stop? Hold back, so we also may speak.
Why have we been silenced like beasts before you?
Wrath has used you. For what, if you die, will what is under heaven be uninhabited, or mountains overturned from foundations?
But light of ungodly will be quenched, and flame of theirs will not blaze forth.
His light is darkness in his dwelling, and lamp over him will be extinguished.
Let smallest things hunt down his possessions, and his counsel slip.
His foot is cast into snare, and let him be twisted in net.
Let traps come upon him, and let thirsty ones overpower him.
His rope is hidden in ground, and his capture on paths.
Let pains destroy him around, and let many come about his feet in hunger.
An extraordinary corpse has been prepared for him.
Let branches of his feet be eaten, and let death devour his beauties.
Let healing be torn from his dwelling, and let royal necessity seize him.
It will lodge in his tent in his night; his fair things will be scattered with sulfur.
His roots below will be dried up, and above his harvest will fall.
His memorial perish from earth, and let there be no name of his on outside.
Let him be driven from light into darkness.
He will not be known among his people, nor saved under heaven his house; others will live in what is his.
Last ones groaned over him, and first ones were seized with amazement.
These are houses of unjust men, and this is place of those not knowing Lord.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
Until when will you trouble my soul and tear me down with words?
Know only that Lord did this to me. Speaking against me, not ashamed, you press upon me.
Yes then, if in truth I went astray, my wandering lodges with me. To speak word not needed, my words wander and not in season.
If indeed you magnify yourselves against me and throw reproach at me,
know then that Lord is one who troubled me and raised his stronghold over me.
Behold, I laugh at reproach and will not speak; I will cry out, and there is nowhere judgment.
All around I am walled in, and I will certainly not pass; over my face he set darkness.
He stripped glory from me and took crown from my head.
He tore me apart round about, and I am gone; he cut off my hope like tree.
He used wrath terribly against me and regarded me like enemy.
His raiding bands came together against me; they encircled me in ambushes on my paths.
My brothers stood far from me, and they knew me as stranger; my friends became without mercy.
My nearest ones did not acknowledge me, and those knowing my name forgot me.
Neighbors of my house and my servant girls treated me as stranger before them.
I called my servant, and he did not obey; my mouth pleaded with him.
And I begged my wife, and flattering, I was calling sons of my concubines.
Those forever rejected me; when I rise, they speak against me.
Those who knew me abhorred me; those I had loved rose against me.
My flesh rotted upon my skin, and my bones are held in my teeth.
Pity me, pity me, O friends, for hand of Lord is what touched me.
Why do you persecute me as Lord does, and are not filled from my flesh?
If only someone would grant my words be written, and set down in book forever,
engraved with iron stylus and lead, or cut into rocks.
For I know that one about to free me is eternal, and upon earth
he will raise up my skin enduring these things, for from Lord these things were accomplished for me.
Which things I know in myself, which my eye has seen and not another; all things have been fulfilled for me in my bosom.
But if you say, What shall we say against him, and we will find root of matter in him,
then you also beware of covering; for wrath will come upon lawless men, and then they will know where their substance is.
And taking up the matter, Sophar the Minaian says,
Did I not suppose you would answer back thus? Do you not understand more than I do?
I will hear discipline of my shame, and spirit from my understanding answers me.
Do you not know these things from long ago, from when man was placed upon earth,
that gladness of ungodly is sudden fall, and joy of lawless men destruction?
If his gifts go up to heaven and his sacrifice touches clouds,
then when he thinks he is already established, he will utterly perish, and those who saw him will say, Where is he?
Like dream flown away, he will not be found; he flew off like night phantom.
Eye passed by him and will not continue, and his place will not notice him anymore.
Let lesser men destroy his sons, and his hands kindle pains.
His bones were filled with youth, and with him it will lie down in dust.
If evil be sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.
He will not spare it and will not abandon it, but hold it fast in midst of his throat.
And he will not be able to help himself; venom of asp is in his belly.
Wealth unjustly gathered will be vomited out; angel will drag him from his house.
Let him suck wrath of dragons, and tongue of serpent will kill him.
Let him not see milking of nomads, nor pastures of honey and butter.
He labored for empty and vain things; wealth from which he will not taste, like twisted thing unchewed and unswallowable.
For he crushed houses of many weak ones, and seized dwelling he did not build.
There is no salvation for his possessions; in his desire he will not be saved.
There is no remnant for his foods; therefore his good things will not flourish.
And when he thinks he is already full, he will be distressed, and every necessity will come upon him.
Wrath of anger will be sent upon him and pains washed upon him, if only to fill his belly.
And he will not be saved from hand of iron; bronze bow will wound him.
Let arrow go through his body, and let lightnings walk in his dwelling; fears upon him.
Let all darkness wait for him; unquenchable fire will devour him, and stranger will afflict his house.
Heaven will reveal his lawless acts, and earth rise up against him.
Destruction will drag away his house; final end, day of wrath will come upon him.
This is portion of ungodly man from Lord, and possession of his goods from the Overseer.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
Hear, hear my words, so that this from you may be my consolation.
Bear with me, and I will speak; then afterward laugh at me.
For is my reproof against man? And why should I not be angry?
Looking at me, be amazed, laying hand upon cheek.
For if I remember, I hurried, and pains seized my flesh.
Why do ungodly men live, grow old, and even abound in wealth?
Their offspring remain with them, and their children before their eyes.
Their houses prosper, and fear is nowhere; scourge from Lord is not upon them.
Their cow did not miscarry; what was in womb was preserved and did not fail.
And they remain like perpetual sheep, and their little children play.
Taking up psaltery and harp, they rejoice at sound of song.
They completed their life in good things, and in rest of Hades they fell asleep.
Yet they say to Lord, Depart from me; I do not want to know your ways.
What is Sufficient One, that we should serve him, and what profit if we meet him?
For their good things were in their hands, but he does not regard works of ungodly men.
Yet lamp of ungodly men will be quenched, and destruction will come upon them, and pains will hold them from wrath.
And they will be like chaff before wind, or like dust that whirlwind carried off.
Let his possessions fail his sons; he will repay it to him, and he will know.
Let his eyes see his own slaughter, and let him not be rescued from Lord.
For what is his will in his house after him, when numbers of his months were divided?
Is it not Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge? He judges murders.
This man will die in strength of his simplicity, altogether prosperous and flourishing.
His inward parts are full of fat, and his marrow pours out.
But another dies in bitterness of soul, not having eaten any good thing.
Yet together they lie down on earth, and rot covered them.
So I know that you boldly press upon me.
For you will say, Where is house of ruler, and where is shelter of tents of ungodly men?
Ask those passing along way, and you will not reject their signs.
For wicked man is spared in day of destruction; they will be led away in day of his wrath.
Who will declare his way to his face? And what he did, who will repay to him?
And he was carried off to tombs, and kept watch over on mound.
Pebbles of torrent were sweet to him, and after him every man will depart, and before him were beyond number.
How then do you comfort me with empty things? To make me cease from you, nothing remains.
And taking up the matter, Eliphas the Thaimanite says,
Is it not Lord who teaches understanding and knowledge?
For what does it matter to Lord if you were blameless in works, or what profit if you made your way simple?
Will he reprove you because he takes account of your words, and enter judgment with you?
Is not your evil great, and your sins beyond number?
You took pledges from your brothers for nothing, and stripped clothing from naked men.
You did not give water to thirsty men, but withheld bread from hungry men.
And you admired faces of certain men, and settled those upon earth.
But you sent widows away empty, and afflicted orphans.
Therefore snares encircled you, and extraordinary war made you hurry.
Light turned to darkness for you, and water covered you as you slept.
Is not he who dwells in heights watching, and he humbled those carried in arrogance?
And you said, What did Mighty One know? Does he judge through thick gloom?
Clouds are his hiding place, and he will not be seen; and he walks about circuit of heaven.
Will you keep ancient path which unjust men trod,
who were seized before their time, their foundations a river pouring over?
Who say, What will Lord do to us, or what will Almighty bring upon us?
Yet he filled their houses with good things, but counsel of ungodly men is far from him.
Righteous men seeing laughed, and blameless one mocked.
If indeed their substance did not vanish, and fire will devour what remains of them.
Become firm then, if you endure, and then your fruit will be in good things.
Receive declaration from his mouth, and take his words into your heart.
And if you return and humble yourself before Lord, you made injustice far from your dwelling.
You will place Ophir on rock in dust and as torrent-stones among rocks.
Then Almighty will be your helper against enemies, and will restore you pure like silver refined by fire.
Then you will speak boldly before Lord, looking up to heaven with cheerfulness.
And when you pray to him, he will hear you, and will give you to pay your vows.
And he will restore to you dwelling of righteousness, and upon your ways there will be light.
For he humbled him, and you will say, He acted proudly; but one bent in eyes he will save.
He will rescue innocent one, and be saved through purity of your hands.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
And now I know that my reproof is from my hand, and his hand has become heavy upon my groaning.
Who then would know that I might find him and come to end?
I would state my judgment to myself, and fill my mouth with reproofs.
And I would know words that he will say to me, and perceive what he will tell me.
And if he comes upon me in much strength, then he will not use threats against me.
For truth and reproof are from him, and he would bring my judgment out to end.
For I will go to first things, and I am no longer there; and at last things, what do I know?
When he works on left, I did not grasp it; he will wrap right side, and I will not see.
For he already knows my way, and he judged me like gold.
And I will come forth in his commands; for I kept his ways and will by no means turn aside.
And I will by no means pass beyond his commands; in my bosom I hid his words.
But if he judged thus, who is one contradicting him? For what he himself willed, he also did.
Because of this I hurried at him; being admonished, I took thought of him. Because of this let one make haste from his face; I will consider and be alarmed because of him.
But Lord softened my heart, and Almighty made me hurry.
For I did not know that darkness would come upon me, and gloom covered me before my face.
Why then were seasons hidden from Lord?
But ungodly men crossed boundary, seizing flock together with shepherd.
They drove away orphan's donkey and took widow's ox as pledge.
They turned weak ones aside from right way; together meek ones of earth were hidden.
They went out like donkeys in field against me, going forth to their own labor; bread became sweet to him for younger ones.
Before right time they reaped field not their own, and weak men worked vineyards of ungodly men without pay and unfed.
They put many naked ones to sleep without clothing, and took away covering of their souls.
They are drenched by mountain showers; because they have no shelter, they wrapped themselves around rock.
They snatched orphan from breast, and humbled one who had fallen out.
They put naked men to sleep unjustly, and took away bread from hungry men.
In narrow places they lay in wait unjustly, and they did not know righteous way.
They were cast out from city and their own houses, and soul of infants groaned greatly. Yet why has he not made inspection of these things?
While they were on earth, they did not recognize way of righteousness, nor knew its paths, nor walked them.
But knowing their works, he handed them over to darkness, and in night he will be like thief.
And eye of adulterer watched darkness, saying, Eye will not notice me, and he put hiddenness of face.
In darkness he dug through houses; by day they sealed themselves up; they did not know light.
For morning is to them shadow of death, because he will recognize terrors of shadow of death.
He is light upon face of water; let their portion be cursed upon earth.
And let their plants appear upon dry earth, for they snatched embrace of orphans.
Then his sin was remembered; like mist of dew he became unseen. Let what he did be repaid to him, and let every unjust man be shattered like incurable wood.
For he did not treat barren woman well, and did not pity woman.
But by wrath he overthrew weak men; therefore rising up he will by no means trust in his own life.
Being softened, let him not hope to be healed, but he will fall in sickness.
For his exaltation afflicted many, but he withered like mallow in heat, or like ear of grain falling of itself from stalk.
If not, who is one saying I speak lies and will make my words into nothing?
And taking up the matter, Baldad the Sauchite says,
For what foreword or fear is from him, he who makes whole order in highest place?
For let no one suppose there is delay for raiders; upon whom will ambush from him not come?
For how will mortal be righteous before Lord, or who could cleanse himself, one born of woman?
If he orders moon, and it does not shine, and stars are not clean before him,
how much less man, rot, and son of man, worm.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says,
To whom will you attach yourself, and whom are you about to help? Is it not one of much strength and mighty arm?
To whom did you give counsel? Is it not one of all wisdom? And whom will you follow? Is it not one of greatest power?
To whom did you declare words? And breath of whom is that which came out from you?
Will not giants be brought forth from under water, and its neighbors?
Hades is naked before him, and destruction has no covering.
Stretching out north over nothing, hanging earth upon nothing.
Binding water in his clouds, and cloud was not torn under him.
Holding face of throne, spreading his cloud upon it.
He drew boundary by decree upon face of water, until completion of light with darkness.
Pillars of heaven were spread out and were astonished at his rebuke.
By strength he stilled sea, and by knowledge wounded sea-monster.
And bolts of heaven fear him, and by decree he killed dragon that turned away.
Behold, these are parts of his way, and upon mere drop of word we will hear in him; but strength of his thunder, who knows when he will make it?
And again adding, Iōb said in his opening discourse,
As Lord lives, who has judged me thus, and Almighty, who embittered my soul,
as long as my breath is still in me and divine spirit in my nostrils,
my lips will by no means speak lawless things, nor will my soul meditate unjust things.
Far be it from me to declare you righteous until I die, for I will not put away my innocence.
And clinging to righteousness, I will by no means let go, for I am not conscious to myself of having done improper things.
Yet let my enemies be as overthrow of ungodly men, and those rising against me as destruction of lawless men.
For what hope is there for ungodly man, that he clings, trusting upon Lord? Will he be saved?
Or will Lord hear his petition, or when necessity comes upon him?
Does he have any boldness before him, or when he calls upon him, will he hear him?
But now I will declare to you what is in hand of Lord; what things are with Almighty I will not lie about.
Behold now, you all know that you heap empty things upon empty things.
This is portion of ungodly man from Lord, and possession of tyrants will come upon them from Almighty.
And if his sons become many, they will be for slaughter; and if they grow into men, they will beg.
And those left of him will end in death, and no one will pity their widows.
If he gathers silver like earth, and prepares gold like clay,
righteous men will obtain all these things, and true men will hold his goods.
And his house turned out like moth, and like spider.
Rich man, having lain down, will add no more; he opened his eyes, and he is not.
Pains met him like water, and by night gloom carried him away.
Scorching wind will carry him off and depart, and will winnow him from his place.
And it will hurl itself upon him and not spare; fleeing, he will flee from its hand.
He will clap his hands against him and hiss him out of his place.
For silver has place from where it comes, and gold place from where it is refined.
For iron comes from earth, and bronze is quarried like stone.
He set order for darkness, and he himself searches out every limit, stone of gloom and shadow of death.
Torrent breaks off from dust, and those forgetting righteous way grew weak among mortals.
Earth, from it bread will come out, but underneath it is turned up as by fire.
Its stones are place of sapphire, and its dust has gold with it.
Bird did not know that path, nor did eye of vulture look upon it.
Sons of arrogant men did not tread it, nor did lion pass over it.
He stretched out his hand upon sharp rock, and overturned mountains from roots.
And he broke open whirlings of rivers, and my eye saw every precious thing.
And he uncovered depths of rivers and brought his power into light.
But wisdom, from where was it found? And what place is there for knowledge?
Mortal does not know its way, nor will it be found among men.
Deep said, It is not in me, and sea said, It is not with me.
He will not give enclosure in exchange for it, and silver will not stand as its price.
Nor will it be weighed with gold of Ophir, with precious onyx and sapphire.
Gold and glass will not equal it, and exchange for it is vessels of gold.
Coral and crystal will not be remembered, and draw wisdom above innermost things.
Topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it, nor will it be weighed with pure gold.
But wisdom, from where was it found? And what place is there for understanding?
It escaped every man and was hidden from birds of heaven.
Destruction and death said, We heard its fame.
God well understood its way, and he knows its place.
For he watches all that is under heaven, knowing all things on earth, whatever he made.
Weight of winds and measures of waters,
when he thus made rain and counted it, and path in roaring voices.
Then he saw it and declared it, preparing it and searching it out.
And he said to man, Behold, godliness is wisdom, and to abstain from evils is understanding.
And again adding, Iōb said in his opening discourse,
Who might set me as in months before, in days when God guarded me,
as when his lamp shone over my head, when by his light I walked in darkness,
when I was heavy upon my ways, when God made visitation of my house,
when I was very leafy, and my children round about me,
when my ways were poured out with butter, and my mountains poured out milk,
when I went out early in city, and my seat was set in squares,
young men seeing me hid themselves, and all elders stood up,
and great men stopped speaking, putting finger upon mouth.
And those hearing me blessed me, and their tongue stuck to their throat.
For ear heard and blessed me, and eye seeing me turned aside toward me,
because I rescued poor man from hand of mighty man, and I helped orphan who had no helper.
Blessing of one perishing came upon me, and mouth of widow blessed me.
And I put on righteousness and clothed myself with judgment like double robe.
I was eye of blind and foot of lame.
I was father of weak men, and case that I did not know I searched out.
And I shattered jaws of unjust men, and from midst of their teeth I snatched prey.
And I said, My age will grow old like stem of palm; I will live long time.
My root is opened upon water, and dew will lodge in my harvest.
My glory is fresh with me, and my bow will go in his hand.
Hearing me, they paid attention, and kept silence at my counsel.
And upon my word they added nothing, and they became joyful whenever I spoke to them.
Like thirsty earth expecting rain, so these expected my speech.
If I laugh toward them, they will by no means believe, and light of my face did not fall away.
I chose their way and sat as ruler, and dwelt like king among lone-belted men, as one comforting those in grief.
But now least men laughed at me; now they admonish me in part, whose fathers I despised, whom I did not count worthy of dogs of my flocks.
And strength of their hands, why should it be to me? Completion perished upon them.
In want and famine, barren men, fleeing dry place yesterday, distress and misery,
plucking saltwort upon scrub, whose foods were saltwort, dishonored and made worthless, lacking every good thing, even chewing roots of trees because of great hunger.
Robbers rose against me.
Whose houses were caves of rocks.
Among pleasant-sounding places they will cry out; under wild brush they had their way of life.
Sons of fools and dishonored men, name and fame wiped out from earth.
But now I am their harp, and they have me for byword.
And standing far off they abhorred me, and they did not spare spittle from my face.
For opening his quiver he afflicted me, and they sent away bridle from my face.
On right hand shoot rose against me; they stretched out their foot and made roads of their destruction against me.
My paths were crushed, for he stripped off my garment.
With his arrows he struck me down; he dealt with me as he wished; I am mixed up in pains.
My pains turn back upon me; my hope went away like wind, and my salvation like cloud.
And now my soul will be poured out upon me, and days of pains hold me.
And by night my bones are burned together, and my sinews are dissolved.
In much strength he took hold of my garment; like collar of my tunic it encircled me.
And you counted me like clay in earth, and ash is my portion.
And I cried to you, and you do not hear me; they stood and observed me.
And you came upon me without mercy; with mighty hand you scourged me.
And you appointed me in pains and cast me away from salvation.
For I know that death will wear me out, for earth is house for every mortal.
For if only I might be able to lay hand on myself; and having asked another, he will do this for me.
But I wept over every weak man, and groaned when seeing man in necessities.
But I, waiting for good things, behold, days of evils met me rather.
My belly boiled and will not be silent; days of poverty came before me.
Groaning, I have gone without muzzle; I stood in assembly crying out.
I have become brother of sirens and companion of ostriches.
And my skin is greatly blackened, and my bones from heat.
And my harp turned to mourning, and my song to weeping for me.
I made covenant with my eyes, and I will not think upon virgin.
And what did God divide from above, and inheritance of Sufficient One from heights?
Is it not destruction for unjust man, and estrangement for those doing lawless things?
Does he not see my way and count all my steps?
But if I walked with mockers, and if my foot hurried toward deceit,
let him set me then in righteous balance, and Lord knows my innocence.
If my foot turned aside from way, and if my heart followed eye, and if with my hands I touched gifts,
then let me sow and let others eat, and let me become rootless upon earth.
If my heart followed after wife of another man, and if I sat in ambush at her doors,
then let my wife please another man, and let my little ones be humbled.
For wrath of anger is unrestrainable, to defile wife of man.
For it is fire burning upon all my members, which wherever it comes destroys from roots.
And if I despised case of my servant or my servant girl when they were contending with me,
what then will I do when Lord makes inspection of me, and if he makes visitation, what answer will I give?
Were they not formed in womb as I also was? And were we not made in same womb?
And weak men, whatever need they had, did not fail to obtain it from me, and I did not make eye of widow waste away.
And if I ate my morsel alone, and did not share it with orphan,
for from my youth I reared them as father, and from my mother's womb I guided them.
And if I overlooked naked man perishing and did not clothe him,
and weak men did not bless me, and from shearings of my lambs their shoulders were warmed,
if I lifted hand against orphan, trusting that much help surrounded me,
then let my shoulder fall away from collarbone, and let my arm be broken from elbow.
For fear of Lord constrained me, and because of his burden I will not endure.
If I made gold my strength, or trusted in precious stone,
and if I rejoiced because much wealth came to me, and because I laid hand upon countless things,
or if I saw sun shining, moon waning, for these things are not mine,
and if my heart was secretly deceived, and laying hand upon my mouth I kissed them,
then let this too be counted to me as greatest lawlessness, because I lied against Lord Most High.
And if I became glad at downfall of my enemies, and my heart said, Good!
then let my ear hear my curse, and let me become a byword among my people while afflicted.
And if my servant girls often said, Who would give us of his flesh that we might be very full, because I was good?
Stranger did not lodge outside, and my door stood open to every comer.
And if sinning unwillingly I hid my sin,
for I was not ashamed of great crowd, so as not to confess before them, and if I let weak man not go out from my empty bosom-door,
who would grant one hearing me? And if not, hand of Lord I would have feared. And written indictment I had against someone.
Placing it upon my shoulders, I would read it as crown.
And if, not tearing it up, I repaid nothing taken from debtor,
if ever land groaned against me, and its furrows wept together,
and if I ate its strength alone without payment, and grieving I cast out soul of lord of land,
then let nettle come out for me instead of wheat, and thorn-bush instead of barley. And Iōb ceased from words.
And his three friends were quiet, no longer answering Iōb, for Iōb was righteous before them.
And Elious son of Barachiēl the Buzite of kin of Ram from country of Ausitis was angered; and against Iōb he was greatly angered because he declared himself righteous before Lord.
And against the three friends he was greatly angered, because they were not able to answer contrary things to Iōb, and they made him out to be ungodly.
But Elious waited to give answer to Iōb because they were older than he in days.
And Elious saw that there was no answer in mouth of the three men, and his wrath became angry.
And taking up the matter, Elious son of Barachiēl the Buzite said, I am younger in time, but you are elders; therefore I kept silent, fearing to declare to you my own knowledge.
And I said, Time is what speaks, and in many years they know wisdom.
But spirit is in mortals, and breath of Almighty is what teaches.
Not long-lived men are wise, nor do elders know judgment.
Therefore I said, Hear me, and I will declare to you what I know.
Give ear to my words, for I will speak with you listening, until you test sayings.
And up to you I will understand. And behold, there was none from you reproving Iōb or answering his words.
Lest you say, We found wisdom by adding to Lord.
But you allowed man to speak such words.
They were terrified; they answered no more; words grew old from them.
I waited, for they did not speak, because they stood and did not answer.
And taking up the matter, Elious says,
Again I will speak, for I am full of words; spirit of my belly destroys me.
And my belly is like skin-bag of sweet wine boiling, tied up, or like broken bronze-worker's bellows.
I will speak, that I may have rest, opening my lips.
For I will not be ashamed before man, nor indeed will I feel shame before mortal.
For I do not know how to admire face, else moths would eat even me.
Yet hear my words, Iōb, and give ear to my speech.
For behold, I opened my mouth, and my tongue spoke.
My heart is pure in words, and understanding of my lips knows purely.
Divine spirit made me, and breath of Almighty teaches me.
If you are able, give me answer to these things; endure, stand against me, and I against you.
You were fashioned from clay as I also; from same thing we were formed.
My fear will not whirl you, nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
Still, you said in my ears, and I heard voice of your words,
saying, I am pure, not sinning; I am blameless, for I did not act lawlessly.
But he found complaint against me and counts me as opponent.
And he put my foot in stocks, and watched all my ways.
For how do you say, I am righteous, and Eternal did not hear me? For he is eternal above mortals.
And you say, Why did he not hear every word of my case?
For when Lord speaks once, and second time in dream,
or in nighttime meditation, as fearful dread falls upon men in slumberings on bed,
then he uncovers mind of men; in such kinds of fear he frightened them,
to turn man from injustice, and rescued his body from fall.
And he spared his soul from death and him from falling in war.
And again he reproved him in weakness upon bed, and great number of his bones grew numb.
And he will by no means be able to receive every edible thing of grain, and his soul will desire food.
Until his flesh rots away and his bones are shown bare.
And his soul came near to death, and his life to Hades.
If there are a thousand death-bearing angels, not one of them will wound him, if he understands in heart to turn to Lord and tells man his own blame and shows his folly,
he will hold out against his falling into death, and will renew his body like plaster on wall, and fill his bones with marrow.
And he will soften his flesh like that of infant and restore him as grown man among men.
And when he prays to Lord, things will be acceptable to him, and he will enter with clean face, with confession; and he will repay righteousness to men.
Then man himself will blame himself, saying, What things I completed, and he did not examine me according to what I sinned.
Save my soul from coming into corruption, and my life will see light.
Behold, Mighty One works all these things, three ways with man,
but he rescued my soul from death, so that my life in light may praise him.
Give ear, Iōb, and hear me; be silent, and I will speak.
If there are words, answer me; speak, for I want to justify you.
If not, you hear me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom.
And taking up the matter, Elious says,
Hear me, wise men; you who know, give ear to what is good.
For ear tests words, and throat tastes foods.
Let us choose judgment for ourselves; let us know among ourselves what is good.
For Iōb said, I am righteous; the Lord took away my judgment.
And he lied against my judgment; my arrow is violent without injustice.
What man is like Iōb, drinking mockery like water,
not sinning nor acting ungodly, but sharing road with those doing lawless things, to walk with ungodly men?
For do not say that there will not be inspection of man, and inspection for him from Lord.
Therefore, men of understanding heart, hear me. Far be it from me to act ungodly against Lord, and against Almighty to disturb the righteous thing.
But he repays man according to what each does, and in path of man he will find him.
Do not think Lord will do strange things, or Almighty disturb judgment.
Who made earth? And who made what is under heaven and all things within it?
For if he should wish to hold fast and keep spirit with himself,
all flesh would die together, and every mortal would depart into earth from where he was formed.
But if not, take warning; hear these things; give ear to voice of words.
Look at one hating lawless things and destroying evil men, being eternal and righteous.
Ungodly is one saying to king, You act lawlessly, and Most Ungodly One to rulers.
He who did not feel shame before honorable face, nor knows to give honor by admiring faces of great men.
Their crying out and begging from man will turn out empty to them, for they used lawlessly while weak men were turning aside.
For he is seer of works of men, and nothing of what they do is hidden from him.
Nor will there be place to hide for those doing lawless things.
For he will no longer appoint anything over man, for Lord watches all.
He who grasps unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things without number.
He who makes known their works and turns night, and they will be humbled.
And he quenched ungodly men; they are visible before him,
because they turned aside from law of God and did not know his ordinances,
so as to bring cry of poor upon him, and he will hear cry of needy men.
And he will provide quiet, and who will condemn? And he will hide face, and who will see him, against nation and against man alike?
He reigns over hypocritical man because of hardship of people.
Because one says to Mighty One, I have received; I will not take pledges.
Apart from myself I will see; you show me if I worked injustice; I will add no more.
Will he repay it from you because you rejected it? For you will choose, not I. And what you know, speak.
Therefore men of understanding heart will say these things, and wise man heard my word.
But Iōb did not speak with understanding, and his words were not with knowledge.
Yet learn, Iōb: do not yet give answer like foolish men,
lest we add lawlessness to our sins, and let lawlessness be counted upon us while speaking many words against Lord.
And taking up the matter, Elious says,
What is this you counted in judgment, you who said, I am righteous before Lord?
Or will you say, What shall I do if I sinned?
I will give you answer, and your three friends too.
Look up to heaven and see, and study clouds, how high they are above you.
If you sinned, what will you do? And if you committed much lawlessness, what are you able to do?
Since therefore you are righteous, what will you give him, or what will he receive from your hand?
Your ungodliness is to man like you, and your righteousness to son of man.
Being oppressed by multitude, they will cry out; they will cry for help from arm of many.
And he did not say, Where is God, maker of me, appointing night watches,
distinguishing me from beasts of earth and from birds of heaven?
There they will cry out, and he will by no means hear, because of arrogance of evil men.
For Lord does not wish to see strange things, for Almighty himself is seer.
Of those completing lawless things he will save me. And be judged before him, if you are able to praise him as he is.
And now, because there is no one visiting his wrath, and he did not know the trespass greatly,
Iōb opens his mouth vainly; in ignorance he makes words heavy.
And Elious still added and says,
Wait for me a little longer, that I may teach you, for still there is speech in me.
Taking up my knowledge from far, I will speak righteous things to my works.
Truly my words are not unjust; you understand unjustly.
Know that Lord will by no means reject blameless one, mighty in strength of heart.
He will by no means keep ungodly man alive, but will give judgment to poor men.
He will not take away his eyes from righteous man, and with kings on throne he will set them, and they will be exalted in strife.
And if they have been bound in shackles and held fast in ropes of poverty,
then he will declare to them their works and their transgressions, because they will be strong.
But he will hear righteous man and said that they will turn from injustice.
If they hear and serve, they will complete their days in good things and their years in comeliness.
But ungodly men he does not save, because they were unwilling to know Lord, and because, though admonished, they were disobedient.
And hypocrites in heart will appoint wrath; they will not cry for help because he bound them.
Therefore let their soul die in youth, and their life wounded by angels.
In return for what they oppressed, he will bring out judgment of meek men for weak and powerless men.
And further he deceived you from mouth of enemy: abyss, pouring out beneath it, and your table came down full of richness.
Yet judgment will not fail from righteous men.
But wrath will be upon ungodly men because of ungodliness of gifts which they received upon injustices.
Let not willing mind of prayer turn you aside in necessity when weak men exist, and all strengthening power.
Do not draw out night, for peoples go up instead of them.
But take heed not to do strange things, for because of this I rescued you from poverty.
Behold, Mighty One will strengthen in his strength. For who is ruler against him?
And who is one examining his works? Or who said, You did unjust things?
Remember that his works are great, which men began.
Every man has seen in himself, as many mortals as are being wounded.
Behold, Mighty One is great, and we will not know; number of his years is endless.
Drops of rain are counted for him, and they will be poured out as rain for cloud.

Ancient things will flow down, and clouds cast shadow over countless mortals. He set time for beasts, and they know order of resting place. Over all these things your mind is not amazed, nor does your heart change from body.
And if he understands stretchings of cloud, equality of his tent?
Behold, he stretches water upon it and covered roots of sea.
For by them he will judge peoples; he will give food to one who is strong.
Upon hands he covered light, and commanded concerning it in meeting one.
His friend will announce concerning him, possession also concerning injustice.
And because of this my heart was troubled and leaped from its place.
Hear hearing in anger of Lord's wrath, and meditation will come out from his mouth.
Under whole heaven is his rule, and his light upon wings of earth.
After him voice will roar; he will thunder with voice of his arrogance, and he will not exchange them when he hears his voice.
Mighty One will thunder wondrously in his voice, for he did great things which we did not know.
Commanding snow, Become upon earth, and winter rain, and winter rains of his strength.
He seals every man's hand, that every man may know his own weakness.
And beasts entered under shelter and were quiet on their resting places.
Whirlwinds come from storehouses, and cold from extremities.
And from breath of Mighty One he will give frost, and he pilots water as he wishes.
And choice thing fashions cloud, and cloud will scatter his light.
And he will turn roundabout his circuits by divine counsels into all their works; whatever he commands them, these have been arranged by him upon earth.
Whether for correction, or for his land, or for mercy, he will find him.
Give ear to these things, Iōb; stand still and understand power of Lord.
We know that God set his works, making light out of darkness.
And he knows distinctions of clouds, and extraordinary falls of evil men.
And your garment is warm; yet earth rests quietly.
Will you make firm with him ancient things, strong as vision of molten metal?
Why? Teach me what we shall say to him, and let us stop saying many things.
Did book or scribe stand by me, that standing I should make man silent?
But light is not visible to all; it shines afar in ancient things, like what is with him upon clouds.
From north clouds shine with gold; over these things is great glory and honor of Almighty.
And we do not find another like his strength; judging righteous things, he does not think to hear.
Therefore men will fear him, and wise of heart will fear him.
And after Elioun ceased from speech, Lord said to Iōb through whirlwind and clouds,
Who is this hiding counsel, and holding words in heart, but thinking to hide them from me?
Gird your loins like man; I will ask you, and you answer me.
Where were you when I founded earth? Declare to me, if you know understanding.
Who set its measures, if you know, or who stretched line upon it?
Upon what have its rings been fastened? And who is one laying cornerstone upon it,
when stars were born and all my angels praised me with loud voice?
And I fenced in sea with gates when it rushed out, coming forth from womb of its mother,
and I put cloud as its clothing and wrapped it in mist,
and I put boundaries to it, setting bars and gates around,
and I said to it, Up to this you will come and not pass beyond, but in yourself your waves will be broken.
Or did I arrange morning light for you, and morning-star see its own order,
to seize wings of earth and shake ungodly men out of it?
Or did you take earth, clay, and shape living thing, and set speaking one upon earth?
And you took light from ungodly men, and shattered arm of proud men.
And did you come upon spring of sea, and walk in tracks of deep?
And are gates of death opened to you in fear, and gatekeepers of Hades, seeing you, were terrified?
And did you perceive breadth of what is under heaven? Declare then to me how great it is.
And what land does light lodge in, and what is place of darkness,
if you would bring me to their boundaries and know their paths?
I know then that you were born at that time, and number of your years is great.
And did you come upon treasuries of snow, and see treasuries of hail,
kept aside for you for hour of enemies, for day of war and battle?
And from where does frost come out, or south wind scatter into what is under heaven?
And who prepared channel for violent rain, and way for thunderings,
to rain upon land where there is no man, wilderness where no man exists in it,
to satisfy pathless and uninhabited land and make growth of grass spring out?
Who is father of rain, and who begot clods of dew?
And from whose womb does ice come out, and who begot frost in heaven?
Or does it descend like flowing water, and who froze face of deep?
And did you understand bond of Pleiad, and open barrier of Orion?
Or will you open Mazzaroth in its season, and bring Evening Star with its tail?
And do you know turnings of heaven, or things happening together under heaven?
And will you call cloud with voice, and will trembling of abundant water obey you?
And will you send out lightnings, and they will go and say to you, What is it?
And who gave women skill in weaving, or embroidered knowledge?
And who counts clouds in wisdom, and bent heaven down to earth,
and it was poured out like dusty earth, and I glued it together like stone cube?
And will you hunt food for lions, and fill souls of dragons,
for they fear in their lairs and sit in woods lying in wait?
And who prepared food for raven? For its young cry to Lord, wandering and seeking food.
Do you know time of giving birth of rock-goats, and did you watch birth-pangs of hinds?
And did you count full months of their bearing, and loosen their pangs?
And did you rear their young without fear, and send out their birth-pangs?
Their young will burst forth, increase with produce, go out and by no means return to them.
And who let wild donkey go free, and who loosed its bonds?
And I set its dwelling in wilderness, and its tents in salt land.
Laughing at tumult of city, and not hearing rebuke of tax-collector,
it will inspect mountains for its pasture and seek after every green thing.
Will unicorn be willing to serve you, or sleep at your manger?
And will you bind its yoke with straps, or will it drag your furrows in plain?
And do you trust in it because its strength is great? And will you leave your works to it?
And will you trust that it will return your seed and bring it into your threshing floor?
Wing of rejoicing ostriches, if it should conceive stork and hawk,
because it will leave its eggs in earth and brood them upon dust,
and forgot that foot will scatter them and beasts of field trample them.
It hardened its young so as not to be its own; for nothing it labored without fear,
because God made wisdom silent to it and did not divide understanding to it.
At time on high it will raise itself up; it will laugh at horse and its rider.
And did you clothe horse with strength, and put fear on its neck?
And did you put armor on it, and boldness on its chest?
Pawing in plain in pride, it goes out to field in strength.
Meeting arrow, it laughs and will by no means turn back from iron.
Over it boast bow and sword.
And anger will destroy earth, and it will by no means believe until trumpet sounds.
And when trumpet sounds it says, Good! And from far off it smells war with leap and cry.
And by your knowledge has hawk stood still, spreading out wings motionless and looking southward?
And by your command does eagle rise up, and vulture, sitting, lodge at its nest?
Upon projection of rock and hidden place.
From there, being there, it seeks foods; its eyes watch from far away.
And its young wallow in blood, and wherever corpses are, they are immediately found.
And Lord God answered Iōb and said,
Will one turning aside judgment with Sufficient One, reproving God, answer this?
And taking up the matter, Iōb says to Lord,
Why am I still judged, being admonished and reproving Lord, hearing such things while I am nothing? What answer shall I give to these things? I will put hand on my mouth.
Once I spoke, but on second time I will not add.
And again taking up the matter, Lord said to Iōb out of cloud,
But gird your loins like man; I will ask you, and you answer me.
Do not reject my judgment; do you think I have dealt with you otherwise than that you might appear righteous?
Or is arm of yours against Lord, or your voice thundering against him?
Take up then height and power, and clothe yourself with glory and honor.
And send out angels in wrath, and humble every arrogant man.
And quench proud man, and rot ungodly men at once.
Hide them together outside in earth, and fill their faces with dishonor.
Then I too will confess that your right hand can save.
But now behold beasts beside you; it eats grass like oxen.
Behold then its strength upon loins, and its power upon navel of belly.
It set tail like cypress, and its sinews are interwoven.
Its ribs are bronze ribs, and its backbone cast iron.
This is beginning of Lord's creation, made to be mocked by his angels.
And going upon steep mountain, it made joy for quadrupeds in Tartarus.
It sleeps under every kind of tree, beside papyrus and reed and rush.
And great trees shade it, with branches and shoots of agnus-tree.
If flood happens, it will not notice; it trusts that Jordan will dash into its mouth.
Will one take it in its eye? With snare one will pierce its nose.
And will you lead dragon with hook, and put halter around its nose?
Or will you bind ring in its nostril and pierce its lip with bracelet?
And will it speak to you with petition, making supplications softly?
And will it make covenant with you, and you will take it for eternal slave?
And will you play with it like bird, or bind it like sparrow for child?
And nations feed upon it, and races of Phoenicians divide it up.
And all ships gathered together will by no means carry one skin of its tail, nor in fishing boats its head.
And will you lay hand upon it, remembering war happening in its body, and let it happen no more?
Have you not seen it, nor marveled at things spoken of it?
Have you not feared because it has been prepared for me? For who is one standing against me?
Or who will withstand me and endure, if all that is under heaven is mine?
I will not be silent because of it, and word of power will have mercy on its equal.
Who will uncover face of its clothing? And who would enter fold of its breastplate?
Who will open gates of its face? Around its teeth is fear.
Its inward parts are bronze shields, and its binding like emery stone.
One cleaving to another, and breath will by no means pass through it.
A man to his brother will be glued; they hold together and will by no means be torn apart.
At its sneezing light shines, and its eyes like form of morning star.
From its mouth go out burning lamps, and hearths of fire are scattered abroad.
From its nostrils comes out smoke of furnace burning with coals of fire.
Its soul is coals, and flame goes out from its mouth.
And in its neck strength lodges; destruction runs before it.
Fleshes of its body are joined together; he will pour upon it, and it will not be shaken.
Its heart is fixed like stone, standing like unhammersmitten anvil.
When it turns, there is fear to beasts, to quadrupeds on earth leaping.
If spears meet it, they will do nothing, nor raised spear and breastplate.
For it counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.
Bronze bow will by no means wound it; it counts stone-slinger as grass.
Hammers were counted as reed, and it laughs at shaking of fire-bearer.
Its bed is sharp spits, and all gold of sea under it like immeasurable clay.
It makes deep boil like bronze pot, and counts sea like perfume-vessel.
And Tartarus of deep it counted like captive, and deep for its walking.
There is nothing upon earth like it, made to be mocked by my angels.
It sees every high thing; and it is king of all things in waters.
And taking up the matter, Iōb says to Lord,
I know that you can do all things, and nothing is impossible for you.
For who is one hiding counsel from you, sparing words, and thinking to hide you? And who will tell me things I did not know, great and wonderful things which I did not understand?
Hear me, Lord, that I too may speak; I will ask you, and you teach me.
By hearing of ear I formerly heard you, but now my eye has seen you.
Therefore I despised myself and melted away, and I count myself earth and ashes.
And it happened after Lord spoke all these words to Iōb, Lord said to Eliphas the Thaimanite, You and your two friends sinned, for you spoke nothing true before me, as my servant Iōb did.

Now then take seven calves and seven rams and go to my servant Iōb, and he will make fruit-offering concerning you. And my servant Iōb will pray concerning you, because unless I receive his face, for his sake I would have destroyed you, for you did not speak truth concerning my servant Iōb.
And Eliphas the Thaimanite and Baldad the Sauchite and Sophar the Minaian went and did as Lord instructed them, and through Iōb he loosed their sin.
And Lord increased Iōb. And when he prayed also concerning his friends, he forgave them their sin. And Lord gave double whatever had been before Iōb, for doubling.

And all his brothers and sisters heard all things that happened to him, and they came to him, and all who had known him from first. And eating and drinking with him, they comforted him and marveled over all that Lord brought upon him. And each gave him one lamb and a gold four-drachma piece unstamped.
And Lord blessed last things of Iōb more than former things. And his livestock was fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, one thousand yoke of oxen, and one thousand female grazing donkeys.
And seven sons and three daughters were born to him.
And he called first Day, second Cassia, and third Horn of Amaltheia.
And no women under heaven were found better than daughters of Iōb, and father gave them inheritance among their brothers.
And Iōb lived after the blow one hundred seventy years; altogether he lived two hundred forty-eight years, and Iōb saw his sons and sons of his sons, fourth generation.

And Iōb died old and full of days. And it is written that he will rise again with those whom Lord raises up. This man, interpreted from Syriac book, dwelt in land Ausitis on borders of Idumaia and Arabia, and his former name was Iōbab. Taking Arabian wife, he fathered son whose name was Ennon. And he himself was son of Zare, one of sons of Esau, from mother Bosorra, so as to be fifth from Abraham. And these were kings who reigned in Edom, over which he also first ruled: Balak son of Beōr, and name of his city was Dennaba; after Balak, Iōbab called Iōb; after him Asom, ruler from country of Thaimanitis; after him Adad son of Barad, who cut down Madiam in plain of Mōab, and name of his city was Geththaim. And friends coming to him were Eliphas king of sons of Esau from Thaimanites, Baldad tyrant of Sauchites, and Sophar king of Minaians.
Blessed man who did not walk in counsel of ungodly men, and did not stand in way of sinners, and did not sit upon seat of pestilent men,
but his delight is in law of Lord, and in his law he will meditate day and night.
And he will be like tree planted by outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and its leaf will not wither, and all things whatever he does will prosper.
Not so ungodly men, not so, but like chaff which wind throws from face of earth.
Because of this ungodly men will not stand in judgment, nor sinners in counsel of righteous men.
For Lord knows way of righteous men, but way of ungodly men will perish.
Why did nations rage, and peoples meditate empty things?
Kings of earth stood by, and rulers were gathered together against Lord and against his Anointed. Interlude.
Let us tear their bonds apart and cast their yoke from us.
One dwelling in heavens will laugh at them, and Lord will mock them.
Then he will speak to them in his wrath and trouble them in his anger.
But I was set as king by him upon Sion, his holy mountain,
declaring decree of Lord. Lord said to me, You are my son; today I have begotten you.
Ask from me, and I will give nations as your inheritance and ends of earth as your possession.
You will shepherd them with iron rod; like potter's vessel you will shatter them.
And now, kings, understand; be instructed, all judging earth.
Serve Lord in fear and rejoice in him with trembling.
Take hold of instruction lest Lord be angered and you perish from righteous way when his wrath is quickly kindled. Blessed all who trust in him.
Psalm of David, when he fled from face of Abessalōm his son.
Lord, why were those afflicting me multiplied? Many rise up against me.
Many say to my soul, There is no salvation for him in his God. Interlude.
But you, Lord, are my defender, my glory, and one lifting my head.
With my voice I cried to Lord, and he heard me from his holy mountain. Interlude.
I lay down and slept; I awoke, because Lord will help me.
I will not fear from myriads of people those surrounding and attacking me.
Rise up, Lord; save me, my God, because you struck all who hate me for nothing; teeth of sinners you shattered.
Salvation belongs to Lord, and your blessing upon your people.
For end. In psalms. Song of David.
When I call, God of my righteousness heard me; in affliction you widened space for me. Have pity on me and hear my prayer.
Sons of men, until when heavy-hearted? Why do you love vanity and seek lie? Interlude.
And know that Lord made his holy one wondrous; Lord will hear me when I cry to him.
Be angry and do not sin; say within your hearts, and upon your beds be pierced through. Interlude.
Sacrifice sacrifice of righteousness and hope upon Lord.
Many say, Who will show us good things? Light of your face, Lord, was marked upon us.
You gave gladness into my heart, from season when their grain and wine and oil were multiplied.
In peace, at same time, I will lie down and sleep, because you, Lord, alone settled me in hope.
For end. Concerning her who inherits. Psalm of David.
Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry.
Attend to voice of my petition, my King and my God, because to you I will pray, Lord.
In morning you will hear my voice; in morning I will stand before you and keep watch.
For you are not God willing lawlessness, nor will one doing evil dwell with you.
Lawless men will not remain before your eyes; you hated all working lawlessness.
You will destroy all speaking lie; man of bloods and deceit Lord abhors.
But I, in multitude of your mercy, will enter into your house; I will worship toward your holy temple in your fear.
Lord, lead me in your righteousness because of my enemies; make your way straight before me.
Because there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat open grave; with their tongues they dealt deceitfully.
Judge them, God; let them fall from their counsels. According to multitude of their ungodliness cast them out, because they embittered you, Lord.
And let all hoping in you be glad; into age they will rejoice, and you will dwell among them; and all loving your name will boast in you.
Because you will bless righteous man, Lord; as with weapon of favor you crowned us.
For end. In hymns. Concerning eighth. Psalm of David.
Lord, do not reprove me in your fury, nor discipline me in your anger.
Have mercy on me, Lord, because I am weak. Heal me, Lord, because my bones were troubled.
And my soul was greatly troubled. And you, Lord, until when?
Turn back, Lord; rescue my soul. Save me because of your mercy.
Because in death there is none remembering you; and in Hades who will confess to you?
I toiled in my groaning; every night I will wash my bed, with my tears I will soak my couch.
My eye was troubled from anger; I grew old among all my enemies.
Depart from me, all working lawlessness, because Lord heard voice of my weeping.
Lord heard my petition; Lord received my prayer.
Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; let them turn back and be greatly ashamed very quickly.
Psalm of David, which he sang to Lord concerning words of Chousi son of Iemeni.
Lord my God, upon you I hoped; save me from all pursuing me and rescue me,
lest he seize my soul like lion, while there is none redeeming and none saving.
Lord my God, if I did this, if there is injustice in my hands,
if I repaid evil to those repaying me, then let me fall away from my enemies empty.
Then let enemy pursue my soul and seize it, and trample my life into earth, and settle my glory in dust. Interlude.
Rise up, Lord, in your anger; be lifted up at ends of my enemies. Wake up, Lord my God, in command which you enjoined.
And gathering of peoples will encircle you, and over this return on high.
Lord judges peoples. Judge me, Lord, according to my righteousness and according to my innocence upon me.
Let evil of sinners come to end, and you will set righteous man straight, examining hearts and kidneys, O God.
My help is righteous from God, the one saving upright ones in heart.
God is righteous judge, strong and patient, not bringing on anger each day.
If you do not turn back, he will polish his sword, stretch his bow, and prepare it.
And in it he prepared instruments of death; his arrows he worked out for burning ones.
Behold, he travailed with injustice, conceived toil, and gave birth to lawlessness.
He dug pit and scooped it out, and he will fall into hole which he made.
His toil will return upon his head, and his injustice will come down upon his crown.
I will confess to Lord according to his righteousness, and I will sing praise to name of Lord Most High.
For end. Concerning winepresses. Psalm of David.
Lord, our Lord, how wondrous your name in all earth, because your magnificence was lifted above heavens.
Out of mouth of infants and nursing ones you prepared praise, because of your enemies, to tear down enemy and avenger.
Because I will see heavens, works of your fingers, moon and stars which you founded.
What is man, that you remember him, or son of man, that you visit him?
You lessened him a little from angels; with glory and honor you crowned him.
And you set him over works of your hands; all things you subjected under his feet:
sheep and oxen, all of them, and also beasts of field,
birds of heaven and fish of sea, things passing through paths of seas.
Lord, our Lord, how wondrous your name in all earth.
For end. Concerning hidden things of son. Psalm of David.
I will confess to you, Lord, with whole heart; I will recount all your wondrous deeds.
I will be glad and rejoice in you; I will sing praise to your name, Most High,
when my enemy turns back. They will grow weak and perish from your face,
because you made my judgment and my case. You sat upon throne, one judging righteousness.
You rebuked nations, and ungodly man perished. Their name you wiped out into age and into age of age.
Swords of enemy failed to end, and you pulled down cities. Their memorial perished with noise.
But Lord remains into age; he prepared his throne in judgment.
And he himself will judge inhabited world in righteousness; he will judge peoples in uprightness.
And Lord became refuge for poor man, helper in opportunities, in affliction.
And let those knowing your name hope upon you, because you did not forsake those seeking you, Lord.
Sing praise to Lord dwelling in Sion; announce among nations his deeds.
Because, seeking out their bloods, he remembered; he did not forget cry of poor men.
Have mercy on me, Lord; see my humiliation from my enemies, you lifting me up from gates of death,
so that I may declare all your praises in gates of daughter of Sion. I will rejoice in your salvation.
Nations were trapped in corruption which they made; in this snare which they hid, their foot was caught.
Lord is known, making judgments; in works of his hands sinner was caught. Song of interlude.
Let sinners turn back into Hades, all nations forgetting God.
Because poor man will not be forgotten to end, and endurance of poor men will not perish into age.
Rise up, Lord; let not man prevail. Let nations be judged before you.
