False witness will not go unpunished; one setting evil ablaze will perish by it.
Luxury does not fit fool, nor if slave should begin to rule arrogantly over rulers.
Merciful man is longsuffering, and his boast comes upon lawless men.
Threat of king like roaring of lion, but his cheerfulness like dew on grass.
Foolish son shame to father, and vows from wages of prostitute not pure.
House and substance fathers divide to children, but fitting wife prepared from God for man.
Cowardice holds down unmanned man, and soul of idle man will hunger.
One keeping command keeps his own soul, but one despising his own ways will perish.
One showing mercy to poor lends to God, and according to his gift he will repay him.
Discipline your son, for thus he will be hopeful; but do not exalt your soul into insolence.
Ill-minded man will suffer much damage; and if he causes destruction, he will add even his soul.
Hear, son, discipline of your father, so that you may become wise at your latter end.
Many reasonings in heart of man, but counsel of Lord remains forever.
Fruit for man = mercy; and better poor righteous than rich liar.
Fear of Lord for life to man, but fear-free man will lodge in places where knowledge is not visited.
One hiding hands in bosom unjustly will certainly not bring them to his mouth.
When pestilent man is scourged, fool becomes more shrewd; but if you rebuke prudent man, he will understand perception.
One dishonoring father and thrusting away mother will be shamed and reproached.
Son, ceasing to keep discipline of father, you will meditate evil sayings.
One guaranteeing foolish child insults judgment, and mouth of ungodly swallows judgments.
Scourges prepared for unrestrained men, and punishments for backs of fools.
Wine unrestrained and drunkenness insolent; everyone mingling with it will not be wise.
Threat of king not different from wrath of lion; one provoking him sins against his own soul.
Glory to man to turn from insults, but every fool entangles himself with such things.
Being reproached, sluggard is not ashamed; likewise borrower of grain in harvest.
Deep water = counsel in heart of man, but prudent man will draw it out.
Great man and precious merciful man, but faithful man = hard work to find.
One walking blameless in righteousness will leave his children blessed.
When righteous king sits on throne, no evil thing stands against his eyes.

Who will boast, "I have pure heart"? Or who will speak boldly, "I am clean from sins"? Lamp of one speaking evil of father or mother will be quenched, and pupils of his eyes will see darkness. Possession hurried at first will not be blessed at last. Do not say, "I will repay enemy," but wait for Lord so he may help you.
Great and small weights, double measures too, both unclean before Lord.
And one doing them will be tripped in his practices. Young man with holy man and straight his way.
Ear hearing and eye seeing, Lord made both works.
Do not love speaking against others, lest you be lifted up; open your eyes and be filled with breads.
Double weight abomination to Lord, and deceitful balance not good before him.
From Lord steps of man are made straight; mortal, how will he understand his ways?
Snare to man quickly to consecrate some of his own things, for after vowing, regret comes.
Wise king winnows ungodly and will bring wheel upon them.
Light of Lord = breath of men, searching storerooms of belly.
Mercy and truth guard king, and in righteousness they encircle his throne.
Adornment of young men = wisdom, and glory of elders = gray hairs.
Blows and bruises meet evils, and wounds into storerooms of belly.
Like rush of water, so heart of king in hand of God; wherever he wills to incline, there he bent it.
Every man appears righteous to himself, but Lord directs hearts.
Doing righteous things and speaking truth more pleasing to God than blood sacrifices.
High-minded in insolence, bold in heart; lamp of ungodly = sin.
One working up treasuries with lying tongue pursues vanities into snares of death.
Destruction will become foreign to ungodly, for they do not want to do righteous things.
Toward crooked men God sends crooked ways, for his works pure and straight.
Better dwell on corner of open roof than in plastered rooms with injustice and common house.
Soul of ungodly will not be pitied by anyone of men.
When unrestrained man is punished, innocent becomes more shrewd; and when wise understands, he will receive knowledge.
Righteous understands hearts of ungodly and brings down ungodly in evils.
One stopping his ears from hearing weak man, he himself will call and there will be no hearer.
Secret gift overturns wraths, but one sparing gifts stirs strong anger.
Joy of righteous = doing judgment, but holy man unclean among evildoers.
Man wandering from way of righteousness will rest in assembly of giants.
Needy man loves gladness; loving wine and oil not for wealth.
Lawless man = purging-scrap for righteous.
Better dwell in desert land than with quarrelsome, talkative, angry woman.
Desired treasure rests on mouth of wise, but foolish men swallow it down.
Way of righteousness and mercy will find life and glory.
Wise man scaled strong cities and pulled down stronghold in which ungodly trusted.
One guarding his mouth and tongue keeps his soul from affliction.
Bold and self-willed and braggart is called pest; lawless is one remembering wrongs.
Desires kill sluggard, for his hands do not choose to do anything.
Ungodly all day desires evil desires, but righteous shows mercy and pities unsparingly.
Sacrifices of ungodly abomination to Lord, especially since they offer them lawlessly.
False witness will perish, but obedient man, being guarded, will speak.
Ungodly man stands shameless in face, but upright man himself understands his ways.
No wisdom, no courage, no counsel against ungodly man.
Horse prepared for day of war, but help from Lord.
Better good name than much wealth, and good favor above silver and gold.
Rich and poor met one another, and Lord made both.
Shrewd man, seeing evil man punished strongly, is himself disciplined; but fools pass by and suffer loss.
Race of wisdom = fear of Lord, and riches and glory and life.
Thorns and snares on crooked ways, but one guarding his soul will keep away from them.
Rich will rule poor, and servants will lend to their own masters.
One sowing base things will reap evils, and will finish off blow of his works. God blesses cheerful man and giver, but vanity of his works he will finish off.
One having mercy on poor will himself be nourished, for from his own breads he gave to poor. One giving gifts acquires victory and honor, but takes away soul of possessors.
Throw pest out of council, and strife will go out with him; for when he sits in council, he dishonors all.
Lord loves holy hearts, and all blameless with lips are acceptable to him; king shepherds them.
Eyes of Lord preserve perception, but lawless man overturns words.
Sluggard makes excuse and says, "Lion in roads; in streets I will be killed."
Deep pit = mouth of lawless man; one hated by Lord will fall into it. There are evil ways before man, and he does not love to turn from them; but one must turn from crooked and evil way.
Folly fastened to heart of youth, but rod and discipline far from him.
One slandering poor makes much for himself, but giving to rich for less.
Incline your ear to words of wise and hear my word, and set your heart on them so that you may know they are good.
And if you cast them into your heart, they will gladden you together upon your lips.
So that your hope may be on Lord, and he may make his way known to you.
And you, write them for yourself threefold for counsel and knowledge on breadth of your heart.
So I teach you true word and good knowledge, to obey by answering words of truth to those putting things before you.
Do not use force against poor, for he is poor, and do not dishonor weak man in gates.
For Lord will judge his case and rescue your unplundered soul.
Do not be companion to hot-tempered man, nor camp together with angry friend,
lest you learn his ways and take snares for your soul.
Do not give yourself as pledge, being ashamed of face.
For if you have nothing from which to pay, they will take bedding from under your ribs.
Do not move age-old boundaries your fathers set.
See man with vision and sharp in his works; he must stand beside kings, not beside sluggish men.
If you sit to dine at table of rulers, intelligently understand things set before you.
And put your hand there, knowing that such things you must prepare.
But if you are more insatiable, do not desire his dishes, for these hold false life.
Do not stretch yourself out, being poor, toward becoming rich; hold back from your own thought.
If you set your eye on it, nowhere will it appear, for wings are prepared for it like eagle, and it returns to house of one leading it.
Do not dine with envious man, nor desire his foods.
For as if someone should swallow hair, so he eats and drinks.
Do not bring him in to yourself and eat your bread with him, for he will vomit it and will damage your good words.
Speak nothing into ears of fool, lest he sneer at your prudent words.
Do not move eternal boundaries, and do not enter possession of orphans.
For Lord, redeeming them, is mighty, and will judge their case against you.
Give your heart to discipline and prepare your ears for words of perception.
Do not hold back from disciplining child, for if you strike him with rod, he will certainly not die.
For you will strike him with rod and rescue his soul from death.
Son, if your heart becomes wise, you will gladden my heart also.
And your lips will dwell within words toward my lips, if they are upright.
Let your heart not envy sinners, but be in fear of Lord all day.
For if you keep these things, offspring will exist for you, and your hope will not depart.
Hear, son, and become wise, and direct thoughts of your heart.
Do not be wine-drinker, nor stretch yourself out in bargaining over meat-purchases.
For every drunkard and fornicator will become poor, and every sleepy one will put on torn and ragged things.
Hear, son, father who begot you, and do not despise because your mother has grown old.
Righteous father rears well, and over wise son his soul rejoices.
Let father and mother rejoice over you, and let one bearing you be glad.
Give me, son, your heart, and let your eyes keep my ways.
For foreign house = pierced jar, and strange well = narrow pit.
For this one will soon perish, and every lawless man will be consumed.
For whom woe? For whom turmoil? For whom judgments? For whom disgusts and babblings? For whom pointless bruises? Whose eyes pale?
Not for those lingering over wines? Not for those tracking where drinking bouts happen?
Do not get drunk with wine, but talk with righteous men and talk in walkings; for if you give your eyes to bowls and cups, afterward you will walk barer than before.
At end, like one struck by serpent he stretches out, and like horned viper venom is poured out for him.
When your eyes see strange woman, then your mouth will speak crooked things.
And you will lie down as in heart of sea and as helmsman in great swell.
And you will say, "They strike me, and I did not feel pain; they mocked me, and I did not know. When will dawn come so that I may go seek those with whom I shall gather?"
Son, do not envy evil men, nor desire to be with them.
For their heart meditates lies, and their lips speak pains.
With wisdom house is built, and with understanding it is set upright.
With perception storerooms are filled from every precious and good wealth.
Better wise man than strong man, and man having understanding than great farmer.
With steering war happens, and help with counseling heart.
Wisdom and good understanding at gates of wise; wise men do not turn aside from mouth of Lord.
But undisciplined men reason in councils; death meets them.
Fool dies in sins, and uncleanness by pestilent man will be defiled.
In evil day and in day of affliction until he should fail.
Rescue those being led to death, and buy back those being killed; do not spare.
But if you say, "I do not know this man," know that Lord of all hearts knows, and one forming breath for all himself knows all, who repays each according to his works.
Eat honey, son, for it is good; comb, so that your throat may be sweetened.
So you will perceive wisdom for your soul; for if you find it, your end will be good, and hope will not abandon you.
Do not bring ungodly to pasture of righteous, nor be deceived by filling of belly.
For seven times righteous will fall and rise, but ungodly will grow weak in evils.
If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and in his stumble do not exult.
For Lord will see and it will not please him, and he will turn his wrath away from him.
Do not rejoice over evildoers, nor envy sinners.
For no offspring will come to evil men, and lamp of ungodly will be quenched.
Fear God, son, and king, and do not disobey either of them.

For suddenly they will punish ungodly; punishments of both, who will know? One guarding word will stay outside son of destruction, and one receiving him received him. Let no lie be spoken to king from tongue, and no lie at all should come out from his tongue. For tongue of king a sword, not fleshly; whoever is handed over will be crushed. For if his wrath is sharpened, with sinews he consumes men, and eats bones of men and burns like flame, so that even eaglets are uneatable.
These things I say to you, wise men: to acknowledge and to show partial face in judgment not good.
One saying to ungodly, "You are righteous," will be cursed by peoples and hated among nations.
But those reproving will appear better; upon them will come good blessing.
Lips will kiss one answering good words.
Prepare your works for way out, and get ready for field, and go after me, and you will rebuild your house.
Do not be false witness against your neighbor, nor widen with your lips.
Do not say, "As he treated me, so I will treat him; I will repay him what he wronged me."
Like field of foolish man and like vineyard of man lacking sense,
if you leave it, it will be made fallow and all overgrown with grass, becoming abandoned, and its stone walls torn down.
Afterward I repented; I looked in order to choose discipline.
A little I slumber, a little I sleep, a little I fold hands over chest.
But if you do this, your poverty will come running before you, and your want like good runner.
These undiscriminating disciplines of Solomon, which friends of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out.
Glory of God hides word, but glory of king honors matters.
Heaven high, earth deep, but heart of king unsearchable.
Beat untested silver, and all of it will be cleansed pure.
Kill ungodly men from face of king, and his throne will be set right in righteousness.
Do not act boastfully before king, nor stand in places of rulers.
For better for you to be told, "Come up to me," than for you to be humbled before ruler. What your eyes saw, speak.
Do not fall into fight quickly, lest at end you regret, when your friend reproaches you.
Withdraw backward; do not despise,

lest your friend reproach you and your fight and enmity not depart, but be equal to death for you. Grace and friendship free; keep these for yourself, so that you may not become reproached, but guard your ways peaceably.
Golden apple in necklace of sardius, so to speak a word.
Bound in golden earring and precious sardius, wise word to listening ear.
As snowfall coming in harvest helps against heat, so faithful messenger benefits those sending him, for he benefits souls of those using him.
Like winds and clouds and most visible rains, so one boasting in false gift.
In longsuffering good-way with kings, but soft tongue breaks bones.
If you found honey, eat what is sufficient, lest being filled you vomit.
Bring your foot rarely into your friend's house, lest filled with you he hate you.
Club and sword and sharp-pointed missile, so also man testifying false witness against his friend.
Way of evil and foot of lawless man perish in evil day.
As vinegar draws what is unfitting, so suffering falling upon body grieves heart. As moth in garment and worm in wood, so grief of man harms heart.
If your enemy hungers, feed him bread; if he thirsts, give him drink.
For doing this you will heap coals of fire on his head, and Lord will repay you good things.
North wind stirs clouds, but shameless face stirs tongue.
Better dwell on corner of roof than with scolding woman in common house.
As cool water pleasant to thirsty soul, so good message from far land.
As if someone should stop up spring and spoil water outlet, so it is indecent for righteous to fall before ungodly.
To eat much honey not good, but one ought to honor glorious words.
Like city whose walls thrown down and unwalled, so man who does anything without counsel.
As dew in harvest and rain in summer, so honor not for fool.
As birds fly and sparrows, so empty curse will not come upon anyone.
As whip for horse and goad for donkey, so rod for lawless nation.
Do not answer fool according to his folly, lest you become like him.
But answer fool according to his folly, lest he seem wise to himself.
From his own ways one sending word through foolish messenger makes reproach for himself.
Take away journey of legs and lawlessness from mouth of fools.
One loosening stone in sling resembles one giving glory to fool.
Thorns grow in hand of drunkard, and slavery in hand of fools.
All flesh of fools is storm-tossed much, for their ecstasy is shattered.
As dog when it returns to its own vomit and becomes hateful, so fool, turning in his own evil, returns to his own sin. There is shame bringing sin, and there is shame = glory and grace.
I saw man seeming wise to himself; yet fool had more hope than he.
Sluggard says, sent into road, "Lion in roads, and murderers in squares."
As door turns on hinge, so sluggard on his bed.
Sluggard hiding his hand in bosom will not be able to bring it to mouth.
Sluggard seems wiser to himself than one bringing message back in fullness.
Like one holding tail of dog, so one standing over stranger's judgment.
As those being healed throw words at men, but one answering to word first will be tripped,
so all ambushing their own friends; when seen, they say, "I acted in play."
With much wood fire flourishes, but where there is no double-tongued man, fight grows quiet.
Brazier for coals and wood for fire, and scolding man for turmoil of fight.
Words of whisperers soft, yet these strike into storerooms of inward parts.
Silver given with deceit should be considered potsherd; smooth lips cover grieving heart.
With lips enemy nods agreement about everything, but in heart he devises deceits.
If enemy begs you with loud voice, do not be persuaded, for seven evils are in his soul.
One hiding enmity sets deceit together, but making his own sins plain is known in councils.
One digging pit for neighbor will fall into it, and one rolling stone rolls it on himself.
Lying tongue hates truth, and unchecked mouth makes disorders.
Do not boast about things for tomorrow, for you do not know what next day will bring forth.
Let neighbor praise you, not your own mouth; stranger, not your own lips.
Heavy stone and burdensome sand, but anger of fool heavier than both.
Pitiless wrath and sharp anger, but jealousy no one withstands.
Better revealed rebukes than hidden friendship.
Wounds of friend more trustworthy than willing kisses of enemy.
Soul in fullness mocks honeycombs, but to needy soul even bitter things seem sweet.
As when bird flies down from its own nest, so man enslaves himself when alienated from his own places.
With perfumes and wines and incense heart delights, but soul is torn apart by mishaps.
Do not forsake your friend or ancestral friend, and do not enter house of your brother when unfortunate. Better nearby friend than brother dwelling far away.
Become wise, son, so that your heart may rejoice, and turn reproachful words away from yourself.
Shrewd man hid himself when evils came on; fools, coming on, will pay damage.
Take away his garment, for insolent man passed by, who destroys strangers' things.
Whoever blesses friend early in morning with loud voice will seem no different from one cursing.
Drops drive man out of his house in winter day; likewise scolding woman from her own house.
North wind hard wind, yet by name is called dexterous.
Iron sharpens iron, and man sharpens face of companion.
One planting fig tree will eat its fruits, and one guarding his own master will be honored.
As faces are not alike to faces, so neither thoughts of men.
Hades and destruction are not filled up; likewise eyes of men insatiable. One fixing eye is abomination to Lord, and undisciplined men unrestrained in tongue.
Testing for silver and refining for gold, but man tested through mouth of those praising him. Heart of lawless man seeks evils, but upright heart seeks knowledge.
If you scourge fool in midst of council dishonoring him, you still will not strip away his folly.
Know well souls of your flock, and set your heart on your herds,
because strength and power not forever for man, nor does he hand down from generation to generation.
Take care of greens in field and you will cut grass, and gather mountain hay,
so that you may have sheep for clothing; honor field so that lambs may be yours.
Son, from me you have strong sayings for your life and for life of your attendants.
Ungodly flees with none pursuing, but righteous trusts like lion.
Through sins of ungodly judgments are stirred up, but shrewd man will quench them.
Strong man in ungodliness slanders poor; like sweeping and useless rain.
Those forsaking law praise ungodliness, but those loving law wrap wall around themselves.
Evil men will not understand judgment, but those seeking Lord will understand in everything.
Better poor man walking in truth than rich liar.
Understanding son keeps law, but one shepherding prodigality dishonors father.
One multiplying wealth with interest and increase gathers it for one showing mercy to poor.
One turning his ear away from hearing law, even his prayer is abominated.
One leading upright astray in evil way will himself fall into corruption; but lawless will pass by good things and not enter into them.
Rich man wise to himself, but poor understanding man will expose him.
Through help of righteous much glory comes, but in places of ungodly men are caught.
One covering his ungodliness will not prosper, but one confessing rebukes will be loved.
Blessed man who trembles always in reverence, but hardening heart will fall into evils.
Hungry lion and thirsty wolf = tyrant, being poor, over needy people.
King lacking revenues = great slanderer, but one hating injustice will live long time.
One guaranteeing man guilty of murder will be fugitive and not in safety. Discipline your son and he will love you and give adornment to your soul; he will not listen to lawless nation.
One walking justly is helped, but one walking in crooked ways will be entangled.
One working his own land will be filled with breads, but one pursuing idleness will be filled with poverty.
Faithful man will be greatly blessed, but evil man will not go unpunished.
One not respecting faces of righteous is not good; such man will be sold for morsel of bread.
Envious man hurries to become rich and does not know that merciful man will master him.
One reproving ways of man will have more favor than one flattering with tongue.
One casting away father or mother and thinking he does not sin = partner of ungodly man.
Faithless man judges vainly, but one trusting in Lord will be diligent.
One trusting in bold heart, that man fool; but one walking in wisdom will be saved.
One giving to poor will not be in need, but one turning away his eye will be in much want.
In places of ungodly righteous groan, but in their destruction righteous will multiply.
Better man rebuking stiff-necked man; for when he suddenly catches fire, there is no healing.
When righteous are praised, peoples rejoice; but when ungodly rulers rule, men groan.
When man loves wisdom, his father rejoices; but one shepherding prostitutes destroys wealth.
Righteous king raises up land, but lawless man digs it down.
One preparing net on face of his own friend wraps it around his own feet.
For sinful man great snare, but righteous will be in joy and gladness.
Righteous knows how to judge poor men, but ungodly does not understand knowledge, and for poor man there is no discerning mind.
Lawless men set city on fire, but wise men turned wrath back.
Wise man will judge nations, but base man growing angry is laughed at and does not shrink back.
Men partakers of blood hate holy man, but upright will seek his soul.
Cowardice upon her the heart of her husband trusts, and such woman will not lack good spoils.

For she works all good things for her husband throughout life.
For she works all good things for her husband throughout life.
She chewed wool and flax and made them useful with her hands.
She chewed wool and flax and made them useful with her hands.
She became like trading ship from far away and gathers wealth for herself.
She became like trading ship from far away and gathers wealth for herself.
She rises from nights and gave food to house and tasks to maidservants.
She rises from nights and gave food to house and tasks to maidservants.
Having looked at field, she bought it, and from fruits of her hands planted possession.
Having looked at field, she bought it, and from fruits of her hands planted possession.
Girding her waist strongly, she braced her arms for work.
Girding her waist strongly, she braced her arms for work.
She tasted that working is good, and her lamp is not extinguished whole night.
She tasted that working is good, and her lamp is not extinguished whole night.
She stretches forearms to useful things, and braces her hands to spindle.
She stretches forearms to useful things, and braces her hands to spindle.
And she opened hands to poor, and stretched out fruit to needy.
And she opened hands to poor, and stretched out fruit to needy.
Her husband does not worry about those in house when he delays somewhere, for all from her are clothed.
Her husband does not worry about those in house when he delays somewhere, for all from her are clothed.

Her husband becomes conspicuous in gates whenever he sits in council with elders dwelling in land.
Her husband becomes conspicuous in gates whenever he sits in council with elders dwelling in land.

She made linens and sold them, and belts for Canaanites.

She put on strength and dignity and rejoiced in latter days.

Her mouth opened attentively and lawfully, and she sent order upon her tongue.
Abomination to righteous = unjust man; and to lawless man, straightening way. Who will find brave woman? Such woman more precious than precious stones.
Abomination to righteous = unjust man; and to lawless man, straightening way. Who will find brave woman? Such woman more precious than precious stones.
Her mouth opens wisely and lawfully; her mercy raised up her children and they became rich, and her husband praised her.
Many daughters acquired wealth, many made strength, but you excel and have surpassed all.
False are charms and vain beauty of woman; for prudent woman is blessed; let her praise fear of Lord.
Give her from fruits of her lips, and let her husband be praised in gates.
My words, son, fear and receive them, and repent. These says the man to those trusting in God, and I stop.
For I am most foolish of all men, and understanding of men is not in me.
But God taught me wisdom, and I knew knowledge of holy ones.
Who ascended into heaven and came down? Who gathered winds in bosom? Who wrapped water in garment? Who held all ends of earth? What name to him, or what name to his children, so that you may know?
All words of God refined; and he defends those revering him.
Do not add to his words, lest he reprove you and you become liar.
Two things I ask from you; do not take grace from me before my dying:
Make vain word and lie far from me; riches and poverty do not give me, but appoint for me necessary and self-sufficient things,
lest being filled I become liar and say, "Who sees me?" Or becoming poor I steal and swear by name of God.
Do not hand servant over into hands of master, lest he curse you and you vanish.
Evil offspring curses father and does not bless mother.
Evil offspring judges itself righteous, but has not washed its own filth away.
Evil offspring has lofty eyes, and its eyelids lift themselves up.
Evil offspring has swords for teeth and grinders like knives, so as to consume humble from earth and poor among men.
Leech had three daughters dearly loved, and these three did not fill her, and fourth was not satisfied to say, "Enough."
Hades and desire of woman and Tartarus and land not filled with water, and water and fire will never say, "Enough."
Eye mocking father and dishonoring old age of mother, ravens from ravines may pluck it out and eaglets may devour it.
Three things are impossible for me to understand, and fourth I do not know:
tracks of eagle flying, and ways of serpent on rock, and paths of ship voyaging sea, and ways of man in youth.
Such way of adulterous woman: when she acts, having washed herself, she says she did nothing improper.
By three things earth is shaken, and fourth it cannot bear:
if servant reigns and fool is filled with foods,
and maidservant throws out her mistress, and hated woman happens upon good husband.
Four things on earth very little, yet wiser than wise men:
ants, though they have no strength, prepare food in summer;
and rock-badgers, nation not strong, who made houses in rocks;
locust has no king, yet marches orderly at one command;
and lizard bracing itself with hands, though vulnerable, dwells in fortresses of king.
Three things travel well, and fourth walks well:
lion's cub strongest of beasts, who does not turn back nor shrink from beast;
and rooster strutting among females, high-spirited, and goat leading flock, and king speaking publicly among nation.
If you push yourself forward into gladness and stretch out your hand with battle, you will be dishonored.
Milk pressed and there will be butter; if you squeeze nostrils, blood will come out; if you drag out words, judgments and fights will come out.
My words were spoken by God, oracle of king whom his mother taught.
What will you keep, child? What sayings of God? Firstborn, I speak to you, son, child of my womb, child of my vows.
Do not give your wealth to women, and your mind and life to afterthought.
Do everything with counsel; rulers drink wine with counsel, for they are hot-tempered; but let them not drink wine,
lest drinking they forget wisdom and be unable to judge weak men rightly.
Give strong drink to those in grief and wine to drink for those in pains,
so that they may forget poverty and remember troubles no more.
Open your mouth for word of God and judge all soundly.
Open your mouth and judge justly; discriminate for poor and weak.
Who will find brave wife? Such woman more precious than precious stones.
Heart of her husband trusts upon her; such woman will not lack good spoils.
For she works good things for her husband all life.
She chews wool and flax and made them useful to her hands.
She became like merchant ship from far away, and gathers livelihood for herself.
And she rises from nights and gave foods to house and tasks to maidservants.
Having considered field, she bought it, and from fruits of her hands planted possession.
Having girded her waist strongly, she braced her arms for work.
She tasted that working is good, and her lamp does not go out whole night.
She stretches her forearms to useful things, and her hands brace to spindle.
She opened her hands to poor, and stretched out fruit to needy.
Her husband does not worry about those in house when he delays somewhere, for all from her are clothed.
She made double cloaks for her husband, and clothing for herself from fine linen and purple.
Her husband becomes conspicuous in gates whenever he sits in council with elders of land.
She made linen cloths and sold them, and belts to Canaanites.
Her mouth opened attentively and lawfully, and she sent order to her tongue.
She put on strength and dignity and rejoiced in latter days.
Dry are occupations of her house, and she did not eat lazy foods.
But her mouth opens wisely and lawfully, and her mercy raised her children and they became rich, and her husband praised her.
Many daughters acquired wealth, many made mighty things; but you excel and surpassed them all.
False are charms and vain beauty of woman; for prudent woman is blessed. Let her praise fear of Lord.
Give her from fruits of her hands, and let her husband be praised in gates.
Words of Ecclesiastes, son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem.
Vanity of vanities, said Ecclesiastes; vanity of vanities, all things vanity.
What surplus for man in all his toil with which he toils under sun?
Generation goes and generation comes, but earth stands into age.
And sun rises and sun sets and draws to its place,
rising there. It goes toward south and circles toward north; circling its circles the wind goes, and on its circles the wind returns.
All torrents go into sea, yet sea will not be filled; to place where torrents go, there they return to go.
All words are wearisome; man will not be able to speak, and eye will not be filled with seeing, nor ear filled from hearing.
What happened, this will be what happens; and what has been done, this what will be done; and there is nothing fresh under sun.
Who will speak and say, "Look, this is new"? It already happened in ages that came before us.
There is no memory for first things, and even for last things that come there will be no memory for them with things yet to be at end.
I, Ecclesiastes, became king over Israel in Jerusalem.
And I gave my heart to seek out and to inspect in wisdom concerning all things happening under heaven, because evil distraction God gave to sons of man to be distracted in it.
I saw all works done under sun, and look, all vanity and choice of spirit.
What is twisted cannot be adorned, and what is lacking cannot be numbered.
I spoke in my heart saying, "I, look, grew great and added wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem," and my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge.
And I gave my heart to know wisdom and knowledge, parables and skill; I knew that this too is choice of spirit.
Because in much wisdom much knowledge, and one adding knowledge will add pain.
I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you in gladness and see in good," and look, this too vanity.
To laughter I said, "Madness," and to gladness, "What does this do?"

I examined in my heart to draw my flesh into wine, and my heart led in wisdom, and to take hold upon folly until I should see what good for sons of men they will do under sun, number of days of their life.
I magnified my work; I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself.
I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted in them every fruit tree.
I made pools of waters for myself, to water from them forest sprouting trees.
I acquired male servants and female servants, and home-born servants became mine; and much possession of herds and flocks became mine beyond all before me in Jerusalem.
I gathered for myself also silver and gold and treasures of kings and provinces; I made for myself singers and singing women and delights of sons of men, cupbearer and cupbearers.
And I grew great and increased beyond all before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom stood by me.
And all my eyes asked, I did not withhold from them; I did not restrain my heart from any gladness, because my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this became my portion from all my toil.
And I looked on all my works which my hands made and on toil in which I toiled to do, and look, all vanity and choice of spirit, and there is no surplus under sun.
And I looked to see wisdom and wandering and folly, because what kind of man will come after counsel? The things it made.
And I saw that wisdom has surplus over folly as surplus of light over darkness.
Eyes of wise man in his head, but fool walks in darkness; and I knew, yes I, that one meeting meets them all.
And I said in my heart, "As meeting of fool, so also to me it will meet; and why then did I become wise more?" I spoke in my heart that this too vanity, because fool speaks from surplus.
For there is no memory of wise with fool forever, since already days coming all were forgotten; and how will wise die with fool?
And I hated life, because evil to me was work done under sun, because all vanity and choice of spirit.
And I hated all my toil with which I toil under sun, because I leave it to man coming after me.
And who knows whether he will be wise or fool? Yet he rules over all my toil in which I toiled and became wise under sun; and this too vanity.
And I turned to bid my heart farewell concerning all toil in which I toiled under sun.
Because there is man whose toil is in wisdom and knowledge and courage, and to man who did not toil in it he will give his portion; and this too vanity and great evil.
For what comes to man in all his toil and in choice of his heart in which he toils under sun?
Because all his days are pains, and his distraction wrath; even in night his heart does not sleep, and this too vanity.
There is no good in man except that he should eat and drink and show his soul good in his toil; and this too I saw, that it is from hand of God.
For who will eat and who will spare apart from him?

Because to the man who is good before him he gave wisdom and knowledge and gladness, but to the sinner he gave distraction, to add and to gather in order to give to one good before the face of God; because this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
For all things time, and season for every matter under heaven.
Time to bear and time to die; time to plant and time to pull up planted thing.
Time to kill and time to heal; time to tear down and time to build.
Time to weep and time to laugh; time to mourn and time to dance.
Time to throw stones and time to gather stones; time to embrace and time to keep far from embracing.
Time to seek and time to lose; time to keep and time to cast out.
Time to tear and time to sew; time to be silent and time to speak.
Time to love and time to hate; time of war and time of peace.
What surplus to doer in things in which he toils?
I saw distraction which God gave to sons of man to be distracted in it.
Together he made all things beautiful in its time, and also together he gave age in their heart, so that man might not find work God made from beginning even to end.
I knew there is no good in them except to rejoice and to do good in his life.
And also every man who eats and drinks and sees good in all his toil, it is gift of God.
I knew that all things whatever God made, these will be forever; on it there is nothing to add and from it nothing to take away, and God made it so that they may fear before his face.
What came to be already is, and what is to come to be already happened, and God will seek what is pursued.
And further I saw under sun place of judgment, there ungodly, and place of righteous, there ungodly.
I said in my heart, "The righteous and the ungodly God will judge, because season for every matter and over every work."
There I said in my heart about speech of sons of man, that God will sort them out and show that they are beasts, even they themselves.

Because meeting of sons of man and meeting of beast, one meeting for them; as death of this one, so death of that one, and one spirit in all, and what did man have more than beast? Nothing, because all vanity.
All go to one place; all became from dust, and all return to dust.
And who knows whether spirit of sons of man goes upward, and spirit of beast goes down to earth?
And I saw there is no good except that man will rejoice in his works, because this his portion; for who will bring him to see what will happen after him?

And I turned and saw all slanders happening under sun, and look, tears of those slandered, and there is no comforter for them, and from hand of those slandering them = strength, and there is no comforter for them.
And I praised the dead, those already having died, above the living who are still alive until now.
And better than both these, whoever not yet came to be, who did not see evil work done under sun.
And I saw all toil and all manliness of work, that it is jealousy of man from his companion; and this too vanity and choice of spirit.
Fool folded his hands and ate his own flesh.
Better one handful of rest than filling of two hands of toil and choice of spirit.
And I turned and saw vanity under sun:

There is one and there is not second, and indeed son and brother are not to him, and there is no end to all his toil; yet his eye is not filled with wealth. "And for whom do I toil and deprive my soul from goodness?" And this too vanity and evil distraction.
Two are good above one, because they have good reward in their toil.
Because if they fall, one will raise his partner, and woe to the one when he falls and there is no second to raise him.
And also if two lie down, there is warmth to them; but one, how will he be warmed?
And if one overpowers, two will stand against him, and threefold cord will not quickly be torn apart.
Better poor and wise child than old and foolish king who no longer knew how to heed.
Because from house of prisoners he will come out to reign, because indeed in his kingdom he was born poor.
I saw all living who walk under sun with young second one who will stand in place of him.
There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them; yet those last will not rejoice in him, because this too vanity and choice of spirit.
Guard your foot whenever you go into house of God, and draw near to hear rather than to give sacrifice of fools, for they are not knowing to do evil.
Do not hurry with your mouth, and let not your heart hasten to bring out word before face of God, because God in heaven and you on earth; on this let your words be few.
Because dream comes in multitude of distraction, and voice of fool in multitude of words.
Just as if you vow vow to God, do not delay to pay it, because there is no pleasure in fools; whatever you vow, pay.
Better that you not vow than that you vow and not pay.
Do not give your mouth to make your flesh sin, and do not say before face of God that it was ignorance, lest God grow angry at your voice and ruin works of your hands.
Because in multitude of dreams and vanities and many words, instead fear God.
If you see slander of poor man and robbery of judgment and righteousness in province, do not marvel over matter, because high one watches over high one, and high ones over them.
And land's surplus in everything = king over cultivated field.
One loving silver will not be filled with silver, and who loved produce in their abundance? This too vanity.
In multitude of good things, eaters of it multiplied, and what advantage for its owner except seeing with his eyes?
Sweet sleep of servant, whether little or much he eats; but fullness of rich man will not let him sleep.
There is sickness I saw under sun: wealth kept by its owner for his harm.
And that wealth will perish in evil distraction, and he begot son and there is nothing in his hand.
As he came out from his mother's womb, naked he will return to go as he came, and he will take nothing in his toil to go in his hand.
And this too evil sickness: just as he came, so he also will depart, and what surplus to him because he toils for wind?
And indeed all his days in darkness and mourning and much wrath and sickness and bile.

Look, what I saw good, what is beautiful = to eat and to drink and to see goodness in all his toil with which he toils under sun, number of days of his life which God gave him, because this his portion.
And indeed every man to whom God gave wealth and possessions and empowered him to eat from it and to take his portion and rejoice in his toil, this gift of God.
Because he will not remember many days of his life, because God distracts him in gladness of his heart.
There is evil I saw under sun, and it is much upon man.

A man to whom God gives wealth and possessions and glory, so that his soul lacks nothing of all he desires, yet God does not empower him to eat from it, because a foreign man will eat it. This is vanity and grievous sickness.

If man should beget hundred and live many years, and however many days of his years may be, and his soul is not filled from good, and indeed burial did not happen for him, I said stillborn better than he.
Because in vanity it came and in darkness it goes, and in darkness its name will be covered.
And indeed it did not see sun and did not know; rest to this more than to that one.
And if he lived a thousand years twice over and did not see good, do not all go to one place?
All toil of man for his mouth, yet soul will not be filled.
Because what surplus for wise man over fool? Because poor man knows how to walk before life.
Better sight of the eyes than wandering of the soul; this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
Whatever came to be, its name already has been called, and it has been known what man is; and he will not be able to be judged with one stronger than he.
Because there are many words multiplying vanity; what surplus to man?
Because who knows what good for man in life, number of days of his vain life, and he made them in shadow? Because who will tell man what will be after him under sun?
Good name above good oil, and day of death above day of his birth.
Better to go to house of mourning than to go to house of drinking, because this end of every man, and living one will give it to his heart.
Better anger than laughter, because by gloom of face heart will be made good.
Heart of wise in house of mourning, and heart of fools in house of gladness.
Better to hear rebuke of wise than man hearing song of fools.
Because as sound of thorns under cauldron, so laughter of fools, and this too vanity.
Because slander drives wise man mad and destroys heart of his strength.
Better end of matter than its beginning; better patient one than high in spirit.
Do not hurry in your spirit to be angry, because anger will rest in bosom of fools.
Do not say, "What happened that former days were better than these?" because you did not ask about this in wisdom.
Wisdom good with inheritance, and surplus to those seeing sun.
Because in its shadow wisdom = as shadow of silver, and surplus of knowledge: wisdom will give life to its possessor.
See works of God, because who can set in order what God twists?
In day of goodness, live in good, and in day of evil, see: indeed God made this corresponding to that, so that man should find nothing after him.
I saw all things in days of my vanity: there is righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and there is ungodly man remaining in his evil.
Do not become very righteous, and do not make yourself excessively wise, lest perhaps you be stunned.
Do not be very ungodly, and do not become hard, lest you die not in your time.
Good that you take hold in this, and from that do not let your hand rest, because one fearing God will come out with all these.
Wisdom will help wise above ten rulers who are in city.
Because there is not righteous man on earth who will do good and not sin.
And indeed to all words they may speak, do not set your heart, so that you may not hear your servant cursing you.
Because many times your heart will work evil against you, and in many ways it will hurt, because you too cursed others.
All these I tested in wisdom; I said, "I will become wise,"
and it was far from me, far beyond what it was, and deep, deep; who will find it?
I circled, I and my heart, to know and to inspect and to seek wisdom and reckoning, and to know ungodly folly and hardness and madness.
And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart = hunting nets and seines, her hands bonds; good one before face of God will be rescued from her, and sinner will be caught in her.
Look, this I found, said Ecclesiastes, one by one to find reckoning.
Which my soul still sought and I did not find: one man among thousand I found, but woman among all these I did not find.
Except look, this I found: what God made with man = upright, but they sought many reckonings.
Who knows wise man, and who knows explanation of word? Wisdom of man gives light to his face, and hardness of his face will be hated.
Keep king's mouth, and because of word of God's oath do not hurry.
Go from his face; do not stand in evil matter, because whatever he wishes he will do.
As king speaks exercising authority, and who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
One keeping command will know no evil thing, and time of judgment heart of wise knows.
Because for every matter there is time and judgment, because knowledge of man much upon him.
Because there is no one knowing what will be, because as it will be, who will tell him?
There is no man exercising authority over spirit to restrain spirit, and there is no authority in day of death, and there is no discharge in war, and ungodliness will not rescue its possessor.
And with all this I saw and gave my heart to every work done under sun, all in which man exercised authority over man to harm him.
And then I saw ungodly men brought into tombs, and they went from holy place and were praised in city because thus they did; this too vanity.
Because rebuttal against those doing evil does not happen quickly; because of this heart of sons of man was fully assured in them to do evil.
Who sinned did evil from then and from length to him; yet I know that good will be for those fearing God, so that they may fear before his face.
And good will not be for ungodly man, and he will not lengthen days in shadow, because he does not fear before face of God.

There is vanity done upon earth: there are righteous ones to whom it reaches as work of ungodly ones, and there are ungodly ones to whom it reaches as work of righteous ones; I said that this too vanity.

And I praised gladness, because there is no good for man under sun except to eat and to drink and to rejoice, and this will stay with him in his toil all days of his life which God gave him under sun.
In which I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see distraction done upon earth, because even in day and in night there is no sleep in his eyes, seeing.

And I saw all works of God, that man will not be able to find out work done under sun. However much man toils to seek, he will not find; and however much wise man says to know, he will not be able to find.
Because with all this I gave into my heart, and my heart saw all this: righteous and wise and their works in hand of God; yet love and hatred man does not know; all things before them.

Vanity in all things: one meeting for righteous and ungodly, for good and evil, for clean and unclean, for one sacrificing and one not sacrificing; as good one, so sinner; as one swearing, so one fearing oath.
This evil in all done under sun: one meeting in all, and indeed heart of sons of man filled with evil and madness in their heart during their life, and after them = to the dead.
Because for whoever joins with all the living there is hope, because living dog better than dead lion.
Because living will know that they will die, but dead know nothing, and there is no wage for them anymore, because memory of them was forgotten.
And indeed their love and indeed their hatred and indeed their zeal already perished, and there is no portion for them anymore forever in anything done under sun.
Come, eat your bread in gladness and drink your wine in good heart, because God already took pleasure in your works.
At every time let your garments be white, and let oil on your head not fail.

See life with woman whom you loved all days of your life of vanity, those given to you under sun, all days of your vanity, because this your portion in your life and in your toil with which you toil under sun.
All that your hand finds to do, do by your strength, because there is no work and reckoning and knowledge and wisdom in Hades where you go there.

I turned and saw under sun that race not to swift, nor war to strong, and indeed not bread to wise, and indeed not wealth to understanding, and indeed not favor to those knowing, because time and encounter will meet them all.
Because indeed man did not know his time: as fish caught in evil net and as birds caught in snare, as they are trapped, so sons of man are trapped for evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
And this too I saw as wisdom under sun, and it is great to me.
Small city, and few men in it, and great king came against it and surrounded it and built against it great siegeworks.
And he found in it poor wise man, and he will save the city by his wisdom, and man did not remember that poor man.
And I said wisdom good above strength, yet wisdom of poor man despised and his words are not heard.
Words of wise in quiet are heard above cry of rulers among follies.
Wisdom good above weapons of war, and sinner one will destroy much good.
Deadly flies rot compound of perfumed oil; a little wisdom held precious above great glory of folly.
Heart of wise at his right, and heart of fool at his left.
And indeed on road whenever fool walks, his heart will lack, and what he thinks = all folly.
If spirit of ruler rises upon you, do not leave your place, because healing will put great sins to rest.
There is evil I saw under sun, like involuntary thing that went out from face of ruler.
Fool was given in great heights, and rich men will sit in low place.
I saw slaves on horses and rulers walking like slaves on earth.
One digging pit will fall into it, and snake will bite one pulling down wall.
One removing stones will be hurt by them; one splitting woods will be endangered by them.
If iron grows dull and he has disturbed its face, then he will strengthen force; and surplus for skill = wisdom.
If snake bites without whispering, there is no surplus for charmer.
Words of mouth of wise = favor, and lips of fool will swallow him.
Beginning of words of his mouth = folly, and last of his mouth = evil madness.
And fool multiplies words; man does not know what has happened, and what will be after him, who will tell him?
Toil of fools will weary them, because one did not know to go into city.
Woe to you, city whose king young, and your rulers eat in morning.
Blessed are you, land whose king son of nobles, and your rulers will eat at right time in strength and will not be ashamed.
In sloth roof-beam will be brought low, and in idleness of hands house will drip.
For laughter they make bread, and wine gladdens living ones, and silver answers all things.
Even in your conscience do not curse king, and in chambers of your bedchambers do not curse rich man, because bird of heaven will carry voice, and winged one will report word.
Send your bread upon face of water, because in multitude of days you will find it.
Give portion to seven and indeed to eight, because you do not know what evil will be upon earth.
If clouds are filled, they pour rain upon earth; and if tree falls in south, and if in north, the place where tree falls, there it will be.
One watching wind will not sow, and one looking in clouds will not reap.
As you do not know what way of spirit, as bones in womb of pregnant woman, so you will not know works of God, who will make all things.
In morning sow your seed, and till evening do not let your hand rest, because you do not know which will prosper, this or that, and if both together good.
And light sweet, and good for eyes to see with sun.
Because even if man lives many years, in all of them he will rejoice, and he will remember days of darkness, because they will be many; all coming = vanity.

Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart do you good in days of youth, and walk in ways of your heart and in sight of your eyes, and know that for all these God will bring you in judgment.
And remove anger from your heart and put evil from your flesh, because youth and folly vanity.
And remember one who created you in days of your youth, until days of evil do not come and years arrive in which you will say, "There is no delight for me in them."
Until sun and light and moon and stars are not darkened and clouds return after rain.
In day whenever guards of house will be shaken and men of strength twisted and grinders cease because they became few and those seeing through openings grow dark,
and doors in market will be shut in weakness of sound of grinder, and he will rise at sound of sparrow, and all daughters of song will be brought low.

And indeed they will look from height and terrors in road, and almond will blossom and locust will grow fat and caperberry will be scattered, because man went to house of his age, and mourners circled in market.
Until silver cord is not overturned and flower of gold crushed and water jar broken at spring and wheel crushed upon pit.
And dust returns upon earth as it was, and spirit returns to God who gave it.
Vanity of vanities, said Ecclesiastes; all vanity.
And beyond that, because Ecclesiastes became wise, he still taught knowledge with people, and his ear traced out ordered parables.
Ecclesiastes sought much to find words of delight, and written uprightness, words of truth.
Words of wise = as goads, and as nails planted, those from gatherings were given from one shepherd.
My son, beware to make many books, there is no end, and much study = weariness of flesh.
End of matter, all is heard: fear God and keep his commandments, because this = whole man.
Because with every work God will bring into judgment, with every overlooked thing, whether good or whether evil.
Song of songs, which is Solomon's.
Let him kiss me with kisses of his mouth, because your breasts are better than wine.
And scent of your perfumes above all spices; your name = poured-out perfume, therefore young women loved you.

They drew you; after you, into scent of your perfumes we will run. King brought me into his chamber. We will rejoice and be glad in you; we will love your breasts more than wine; the upright loved you.
Black I am and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, like tents of Kedar, like skins of Solomon.
Do not look at me because I am darkened, because sun looked past me. Sons of my mother fought in me; they set me keeping vineyards; my own vineyard I did not keep.
Tell me, you whom my soul loved, where do you shepherd, where do you rest at noon, lest I become as one veiled over flocks of your companions?
If you do not know yourself, beautiful among women, go out on heels of flocks and shepherd your young goats by tents of shepherds.
To my mare among chariots of Pharaoh I likened you, my dear one.
How beautiful your cheeks as turtledoves, your neck as necklaces.
We will make for you likenesses of gold with marks of silver.
Until king is at his recline, my nard gave its scent.
Bundle of myrrh my beloved to me; between my breasts he will lodge.
Cluster of cypress my beloved to me in vineyards of En-gedi.
Look, you are beautiful, my dear one, look, you are beautiful; your eyes doves.
Look, you are beautiful, my beloved, and indeed lovely; our bed shadowed.
Beams of our houses cedars, our rafters cypresses.
I = flower of field, lily of valleys.
As lily in midst of thorns, so my dear one in midst of daughters.
As an apple tree among trees of the grove, so my beloved in midst of sons. In his shadow I desired and sat, and his fruit was sweet to my palate.
Bring me into house of wine; arrange love upon me.
Strengthen me with perfumes, heap me with apples, because I am wounded by love.
His left under my head, and his right will embrace me.
I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and by strengths of field, that you not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.
Voice of my beloved. Look, he comes, leaping on mountains, springing on hills.
My beloved is like gazelle or fawn of deer on mountains of Bethel. Look, he stands behind our wall, peering through windows, looking through lattices.
My beloved answers and says to me, "Rise, come, my dear one, my beautiful one, my dove."
Because look, winter passed, rain departed, went away for itself.
Flowers appeared in land, time of pruning arrived, voice of turtledove was heard in our land.
Fig tree brought forth its early figs; vineyards in blossom gave scent. Rise, come, my dear one, my beautiful one, my dove.
And come, my dove, in shelter of rock, close to the forewall; show me your face and let me hear your voice, because your voice sweet and your face beautiful.
Catch for us foxes, little foxes destroying vineyards, and our vineyards are blossoming.
My beloved to me, and I to him, the one shepherding among lilies.
Until day breathes and shadows move, turn back; be like, my beloved, a gazelle or fawn of deer on cleft mountains.
On my bed by nights I sought the one my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him; I called him and he did not answer me.
I will rise now and circle in city, in markets and squares, and seek one my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him.
Watchmen found me, those circling in city: "Did you see one my soul loved?"
Scarcely when I passed from them, until I found one my soul loved. I seized him and will not let him go until I brought him into house of my mother and into chamber of one who conceived me.
I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and by strengths of field, that you not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.
Who is this coming up from wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, from all powders of perfumer?
Look, Solomon's couch: sixty mighty men around it, from mighty men of Israel.
All holding sword, trained in war, each man his sword on his thigh from terrors in nights.
King Solomon made for himself litter from woods of Lebanon.
He made its pillars silver and its recliner gold, its seat purple, its inside paved with love from daughters of Jerusalem.
Come out and see in King Solomon, with crown with which his mother crowned him in day of his wedding and in day of gladness of his heart.
Look, you beautiful, my dear one, look, you beautiful; your eyes doves behind your veil. Your hair like herds of goats that were revealed from Gilead.
Your teeth like herd of shorn sheep that came up from washing, all bearing twins, and barren one not among them.
As scarlet cord your lips, and your speech beautiful; as piece of pomegranate your cheek behind your veil.
As tower of David your neck, built for ranks; thousand shields hang upon it, all darts of mighty men.
Your two breasts like two fawns, twins of gazelle, grazing among lilies.
Until day breathes and shadows move, I will go for myself to mountain of myrrh and hill of frankincense.
All beautiful you, my dear one, and blemish not in you.
Come from Lebanon, bride, come from Lebanon; you will come and pass from summit of Faith, from top of Senir and Hermon, from dens of lions, from mountains of leopards.
You heartened us, my sister bride, you heartened us with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
How beautiful your breasts, my sister bride; how beautiful your breasts beyond wine, and scent of your garments above all spices.
Honeycomb drips from your lips, bride; honey and milk under your tongue, and scent of your garments as scent of Lebanon.
Garden shut, my sister bride; garden shut, spring sealed.
Your shoots = orchard of pomegranates with fruit of choice things, cypresses with nards.
Nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon with all woods of Lebanon, myrrh and aloes with all first perfumes.
Spring of gardens, well of living water and rushing from Lebanon.
Awake, north, and come, south. Breathe through my garden, and let my perfumes flow. Let my beloved go down into his garden and eat fruit of his choice things.
I entered my garden, my sister bride; I gathered my myrrh with my spices; I ate my bread with my honey, I drank my wine with my milk. Eat, companions, and drink and be drunk, brothers.
I sleep, and my heart wakes. Voice of my beloved knocks at door: "Open to me, my sister, my dear one, my dove, my perfect one, because my head filled with dew and my locks with drops of night."
I stripped my tunic; how shall I put it on? I washed my feet; how shall I soil them?
My beloved sent his hand through opening, and my inward parts trembled for him.
I rose, I, to open to my beloved; my hands dripped myrrh, my fingers full myrrh upon handles of lock.
I opened, I, to my beloved; my beloved passed by. My soul went out at his word. I sought him and did not find him; I called him and he did not answer me.
Watchmen found me, those circling in city. They struck me, they wounded me; watchers of walls took my veil from me.
I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and strengths of field, if you find my beloved, what will you report to him? That I am wounded by love.
What is your beloved beyond beloved, beautiful among women? What is your beloved beyond beloved, that thus you bound us by oath?
My beloved white and ruddy, singled out from myriads.
His head gold and fine gold; his curls like palm branches, black as raven.
His eyes like doves by fillings of waters, washed in milk, sitting by fullness of waters.
His cheeks like bowls of spice, growing perfumes; his lips lilies dripping full myrrh.
His hands gold-carved, filled with Tarshish; his belly ivory box on sapphire stone.
His legs marble pillars founded on gold bases; his appearance like Lebanon, choice as cedars.
His throat sweetness, and he whole = desire. This my beloved and this my dear one, daughters of Jerusalem.
Where did your beloved go, beautiful among women? Where did your beloved look away, and we will seek him with you?
My beloved went down into his garden, into bowls of spice, to shepherd in gardens and gather lilies.
I to my beloved, and my beloved to me, one shepherding among lilies.
Beautiful you, my dear one, as Delight; lovely as Jerusalem; awe as battle-lines.
Turn your eyes from before me, because they gave me wings. Your hair like herds of goats that appeared from Gilead.
Your teeth like herd of shorn sheep that came up from washing, all bearing twins, and barren one not among them.
As scarlet cord your lips, and your speech beautiful; as piece of pomegranate your cheek behind your veil.
Sixty queens and eighty concubines and maidens without number.
One is my dove, my perfect one; one to her mother, chosen to one who bore her. Daughters saw her and will bless her; queens and concubines, and they will praise her.
Who is this looking forth as dawn, beautiful as moon, chosen as sun, awe as battle-lines?
Into garden of walnut I went down, to see among produce of torrent, to see whether vine blossomed, pomegranates bloomed. There I will give my breasts to you.
My soul did not know; it set me among chariots of Amminadab.
Return, return, Shulammite; return, return, and we will look on you. What will you see in Shulammite? She comes as dances of camps.
How beautiful your steps in sandals, daughter of Nadab. Curves of your thighs like necklaces, work of hands of craftsman.
Your navel a carved bowl, not lacking mixed wine; your belly heap of wheat fenced round with lilies.
Your two breasts like two twin fawns of gazelle.
Your neck as ivory tower. Your eyes as pools in Heshbon at gates of daughter of multitudes. Your nose as tower of Lebanon watching face of Damascus.
Your head upon you as Carmel, and braid of your head as purple; king bound in flowing locks.
How beautiful you became, and how sweet, love, in your delights.
This your stature was likened to palm tree, and your breasts to clusters.
I said, I will climb the palm tree, I will seize its heights; and now let your breasts be as clusters of vine, and scent of your nose as apples.
And your throat as good wine, going to my beloved in straightness, fitted to my lips and teeth.
I to my beloved, and upon me his turning.
Come, my beloved, let us go out into field, let us lodge in villages.
Let us rise early to vineyards; let us see whether vine blossomed, cypress blossomed, pomegranates bloomed. There I will give my breasts to you.
Mandrakes gave scent, and at our doors every choice fruit, new with old, my beloved, I kept for you.
Who will give you as my beloved, nursing breasts of my mother? Finding you outside I will kiss you, and indeed they will not despise me.
I will take you, I will bring you into house of my mother and into chamber of one who conceived me. I will give you drink from perfumed wine, from juice of my pomegranates.
His left under my head, and his right will embrace me.
I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by powers and by strengths of field: why do you rouse and why do you awaken love until it wishes?
Who is this coming up whitened, leaning on her beloved? Under apple tree I awakened you; there your mother travailed with you, there she travailed, the one who bore you.
Set me as seal on your heart, as seal on your arm, because love strong as death, jealousy hard as Hades; its wings = wings of fire, its flames.
Much water will not be able to quench love, and rivers will not flood it. If man gives all his livelihood in love, despising they will despise him.
Small sister to us, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in day when they speak in her?
If she is wall, we will build upon her battlements of silver; and if she is door, we will engrave upon her cedar board.
I wall, and my breasts as towers. I became in his eyes as one finding peace.
Vineyard came to Solomon in Baal-hamon. He gave his vineyard to keepers; each man will bring in its fruit a thousand of silver.
My vineyard mine before me. Thousand to you, Solomon, and two hundred to those keeping its fruit.
You sitting in gardens, companions attending to your voice, let me hear.
Flee, my beloved, and be like gazelle or fawn of deer on mountains of spices.
Vision which Isaiah son of Amoz saw, which he saw against Judah and against Jerusalem in reign of Uzziah and Jotham and Ahaz and Hezekiah, who reigned over Judah.
Hear, heaven, and give ear, earth, because Lord spoke: Sons I begot and raised high, but they rejected me.
Ox knew one acquiring it, and donkey manger of its master; but Israel did not know me, and people did not understand me.
Woe, sinful nation, people full of sins, evil seed, lawless sons. You abandoned Lord and provoked Holy One of Israel.
Why still be struck, adding lawlessness? Every head into pain and every heart into grief.
From feet to head neither wound nor bruise nor burning stripe; there is no salve to apply, nor oil, nor bandages.
Your land desolate, your cities burned with fire; your country before you foreigners devour it, and it has been desolated, overthrown by foreign peoples.
Daughter of Zion will be left as tent in vineyard, and as watch-hut in cucumber patch, as city under siege.
Unless Lord Sabaoth had left us seed, we would have become as Sodom and been made like Gomorrah.
Hear word of Lord, rulers of Sodom; heed law of God, people of Gomorrah.
What to me multitude of your sacrifices, says Lord? I am full of whole burnt offerings of rams and fat of lambs, and blood of bulls and goats I do not want.
Not even when you come to appear to me. For who sought these from your hands, to trample my court?
You will not continue. If you bring fine flour, it is vain; incense = abomination to me. Your new moons and Sabbaths and great day I do not endure, fasting and idleness.
Your new moons and your feasts my soul hates; you became fullness to me; no longer will I pardon your sins.
When you stretch out hands to me, I will turn my eyes from you; and if you multiply supplication, I will not hear you, because your hands full of blood.
Wash, become clean, remove evils from your souls before my eyes; stop from your evils.
Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue one being wronged, judge for orphan, justify widow.
Come and let us reason together, says Lord. And if your sins are as scarlet, I will whiten as snow; if they are as crimson, I will whiten as wool.
If you are willing and listen to me, good things of land you will eat.
If not willing nor listen to me, sword will devour you, for mouth of Lord spoke these things.
How faithful city Zion became prostitute, full of judgment, in which righteousness slept, but now murderers.
Your silver unapproved, your tavern-keepers mix wine with water.
Your rulers disobey, companions of thieves, loving gifts, pursuing repayment; not judging orphans and not attending to widow's case.
Therefore thus says Master, Lord Sabaoth, Woe to mighty ones of Israel. For my anger will not cease against opponents, and I will execute judgment against my enemies.
I will bring my hand upon you and purge you into purity, but rebellious ones I will destroy; and I will remove all lawless ones from you and humble all proud ones.
I will appoint your judges as before, and your counselors as from beginning; afterward you will be called city of righteousness, faithful mother-city Zion.
For her captivity will be saved with judgment, and with mercy.
Lawless and sinners will be shattered together, and those abandoning Lord will be finished.
Because they will be ashamed over their idols which they wanted, and they were put to shame over their gardens they desired.
For they will be as terebinth that has cast off leaves, and as orchard having no water.
Their strength will be as stalk of tow and their works as sparks of fire, and lawless and sinners will be burned together, and there will not be one to quench.
The word that came from Lord to Isaiah son of Amoz concerning Judah and concerning Jerusalem.
Because in last days mountain of Lord and house of God will be manifest on peaks of mountains, and will be lifted above hills, and all nations will come upon it.

Many nations will go and say, Come, let us go up to mountain of Lord and to house of God of Jacob, and he will announce his way to us, and we will walk in it. For from Zion law will come out, and word of Lord from Jerusalem.

He will judge between nations and reprove many people, and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into sickles; nation will not take sword against nation anymore, and they will certainly not learn war anymore.
And now, house of Jacob, come, let us walk in light of Lord.
For he let go his people, house of Israel, because their land was filled as from beginning with divinations as land of foreigners, and many foreign sons were born to them.
Their land filled with silver and gold, and there was no number of their treasures, and land filled with horses, and there was no number of their chariots.
Their land filled with abominations, works of their hands, and they bowed to what their fingers made.
Man bent down, and male was humbled, and I will certainly not let them go.
And now enter rocks and hide in earth from face of fear of Lord and from glory of his strength when he rises to shatter earth.
For eyes of Lord high, but man low, and height of men will be humbled, and Lord alone will be exalted in that day.
For day of Lord Sabaoth upon every insolent and proud one, and upon every high and lofty thing, and they will be humbled.
And upon every cedar of Lebanon, high and lofty, and upon every oak tree of Bashan.
And upon every mountain and every high hill.
And upon every high tower and every high wall.
And upon every ship of sea and upon every sight of beauty of ships.
Every man will be humbled and height of men will fall, and Lord alone will be exalted in that day.
All handmade things they will utterly hide.
Carrying them into caves and fissures of rocks and hollows of earth from face of fear of Lord and from glory of his strength when he rises to shatter earth.
For in that day man will throw out his silver and gold abominations, which they made to bow to vanities and night-creatures.
To enter hollows of solid rock and fissures of rocks from face of fear of Lord and from glory of his strength when he rises to shatter earth.
Look now, Master Lord Sabaoth will take from Judah and Jerusalem strong man and strong woman, strength of bread and strength of water,
giant and strong man and man of war, and judge and prophet and diviner and elder,
and captain of fifty and wonderful counselor and wise craftsman and understanding listener.
I will appoint youths their rulers, and mockers will lord over them.
People will fall together, man against man and man against his neighbor; child will strike against elder, dishonorable one against honorable.
Because man will seize his brother or one of his father's household, saying, You have clothing, become our leader, and let my food be under you.
He will answer and say in that day, I will not be your leader, for in my house there is neither bread nor clothing; I will not be leader of this people.
Because Jerusalem is abandoned and Judah has fallen, and their tongues with lawlessness speak things against Lord, disobeying, because now their glory was humbled.
Shame of their face stood against them, and their sin they announced as Sodom and made it plain. Woe to their soul, because they planned evil counsel against themselves.
Saying, Let us bind righteous one, because he is inconvenient to us; therefore they will eat produce of their works.
Woe to lawless one; evil will happen to him according to works of his hands.
My people, your exactors glean you, and those collecting dues lord over you. My people, those calling you blessed lead you astray and trouble path of your feet.
But now Lord will stand for judgment and stand to judge his people.
Lord himself will come into judgment with elders of his people and with their rulers: But you, why did you burn my vineyard, and spoil of poor in your houses?
Why do you wrong my people and shame face of poor?
Thus says Lord: Because daughters of Zion were lifted high and walked with high neck and with winks of eyes and in walking of feet dragging tunics together and playing together with feet,
God will humble ruling daughters of Zion, and Lord will uncover their form.
In that day Lord will take away glory of their clothing and their ornaments and braids and hair-nets and crescent-moons,
and the hangings and ornament of their face,
and arrangement of ornament of glory and bracelets and armlets and headdress and wrist-bands and rings and earrings,
and purple garments and garments bordered in purple,
and robes for house and transparent Laconian cloths,
and fine linen and blue and scarlet and linen woven together with gold and blue, and reclining veils.

It will be, instead of sweet smell = dust, and instead of belt you will bind with rope, and instead of golden ornament of head you will have baldness because of your works, and instead of tunic bordered in purple you will gird yourself with sackcloth.
Your most beautiful son whom you love will fall by sword, and your mighty men will fall by sword.
Cases of your ornament will be humbled and mourn, and you will be left alone and dashed to ground.
Seven women will seize one man, saying, We will eat our bread and wear our clothes; only let your name be called upon us; take away our reproach.
In that day God will shine forth in counsel with glory upon earth, to lift up and glorify remnant of Israel.
It shall be that one left in Zion and one left in Jerusalem will be called holy, all written for life in Jerusalem.
Because Lord will wash filth of sons and daughters of Zion and cleanse blood from their midst by spirit of judgment and spirit of burning.

He will come and there will be over every place of Mount Zion and all around her a cloud will overshadow by day, like smoke, and like light of burning fire by night. Over all glory it will be covered.
And it will be for shade from heat and for shelter and hiding from harshness and rain.
